a.notes: The tour camp won this heat for the owner. Its line language (tracks, stops, wires, rails) is what the owner calls high style, and the main camp's grafts made it stronger. Trued took Desk Terminal's moving-coil meter, and it reads native on glass. Departures took Backlit Plate's four-week trace, and it works on the board. Lit Manual took Quote Board's head figures, which work, and the slot trace, which works but leaves the glass half empty. The main camp's crosses gained most where they took lines: Desk's patch lead and rails are its best change. Quote took setup rings and the household row, which work but read as parts more than a system. Settled's quote cords are tidy but slightly pasted (a tiny cord beside every figure). The row afterglow is still invisible in stills on every design. A worrying trend: three crosses (dessau, departures, desk) moved toward monochrome while removing off-period colours, and that undoes the owner's 'not completely monochromatic'. Replace the colour, do not delete it: steel-cyan, sage and wheat in grounded amounts. Glow DNA is well restored in most crosses (lit key word with halo, scanlined tubes, breathing lamps) and is kept to the phosphor.

scores.why: The signature is there, but it is all green glare, near-monochrome (83% green share), and the cards carry no line art or grounded colour. It is the 'Matrix' page the family named.
A real lit terminal beside a calm slate desk, with good glow on the glass and a needle on Status. Line art is limited to a short NOW stub, and 'What's on your mind?' is the title the owner rejected.

The patch lead from the terminal into Coming up's lit NOW rail is exactly the line language the owner loves, and To do hangs from a rail with amber rings. The Plans dial and the new title are real gains. The case is still a slab beside a fairly plain desk, and colour beyond green and amber is scarce.

Confident condensed heads and coloured count figures give the page variety, and the green is kept to the tube. The keycap costume and 'What's on your mind?' count against it, and there is almost no line art.

It is cleaner: the costume is gone, there is a three-ring setup strip, the household index row is good, and the quote heads take one colour per section (heather, wheat, steel-cyan) that supports the green. It still reads as a board of boxes with little line art to lead the eye, and its cells have no phosphor of their own.
A bold poster with real colour variety and a big scanlined lit word. The clay and ochre chat tiles and the card-heavy lower pages drift off-motif, and the title is the rejected one.

The typesetting is the best in the heat: the readout strip with leaders, the waypoint radar and the NOW line on To do. But it cut its colour to near-monochrome (88% green share, hue entropy .23), the opposite of the owner's ask, and on the phone the wordmark is hidden.

The track language runs through every page: the steel branch of starters, Coming up's rail, To do's timetable margin, Chat's spine and the month's rails. Glow is back on the greeting board, and the slate, steel and plum plates are grounded. The Status head is plain.

This is the most owner-shaped page here. The Next up tube stands as the line's lit head with a power wire onto its stop, and the run is lit only to the next stop. Setup is a line of ring stops, Ideas is a line from home at true drive distance, the month carries a lit strip, and Status has a real moving-coil meter on glass. The lines delimit and lead the eye on every page, and graphite and slate ground the rest. The faults: plates stretched to empty graphite, a long title, and on the phone the tube sits low.

A handsome manual. Rails with one lit NOW run through Home, To do and Plans, the figure column brings variety, and the round tubes glow. It is a little cool and diagrammatic, and the lone Fig. panels on the left feel like margin notes.

It has the most varied colour in the heat (hue entropy .58) without losing the green. The welcome slot of four weeks glows with the free weekend in sage, rails now run Settings' numbered parts, Status keeps its wiring figure, and the head figures are typeset well. The tall slot glass is half empty, and Ideas lost its radar emphasis.

Vera's line down the left, with the box as its first stop, is strong line art, and the departures board is good phosphor. The plum and denim starter keys add colour, but the plum is the colour the owner disliked.

The lit wire from the box's ring into the departures board, and the board's four-week trace, are lovely: light where it means now-to-next. The board as the Plans header is a real structure. It went greyer than its parent (71% green, entropy .30), so the off-board page reads monochrome slate.
A well-made sommaire of the whole service, with the VT323 prompt on glass and sized tubes per page. The graphite panels are a bit heavy and boxy, and the line art is thin.

The bare-black panels with one coloured cap feel lighter. The quote heads with a steel cord, the lit Now rail through Plans and the month's Now cell are good grafts, and the glass title with 'plan.' in VT323 is the most CRT-souled greeting here. The page is sparse and somewhat flat beyond the tubes.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the tube as the line's lit head with its power wire, the run lit only to the next stop, the setup line of ring stops, Ideas' line from home, the month strip and the Status meter. Fix: on Home, shrink the stretched plates to their content, or put the next stop's place or weather in the spare graphite. On the phone, bring the tube up under the box, and keep the month strip as a thin trace. On Status, trim the meter case height. The title could tighten to 'Tell Vera what to plan.'. Add one quiet companion colour (the cyan of the plan rings) to the plates' kind line so the desk is not only graphite.

Keep: the four-week slot glass with the sage free weekend, the rails on Settings, the Status wiring figure and the head figures. Fix: fill the slot glass's dark upper half (put the next plan's name on the glass, or make the glass shorter). Give Ideas back a figure with weight beside its list. Make the Plans NOW trace brighter (50%).

Keep: the patch lead from the case into Coming up's NOW lamp, the To do rail with amber rings, the Plans countdown dial and the title. Fix: thin the case further and give its lower half (Ready foot, starters) less slab. Carry rails into Lately added and the kids' wishes, so the desk side is drawn as well. Add a grounded companion ink to the section heads.

Keep: the wire from the box's ring into the board, the board's four-week trace and the board as the Plans header. Fix: bring back colour in the starter stubs and the section roundels (steel-cyan and sage, not plum), so the page off the board is not grey. Separate the row-hover glow from the lit wire (hover in steel).

Keep: the glass title with 'plan.' in VT323, the Now rail on Plans and the household index. Fix: add a rail with stops to To do and Lately added. Give the bare panels a faint top highlight so they read as made surfaces.

Keep: the section-coloured figures, the setup ring strip and the household row. Fix: add a lit NOW rail through Coming up and To do, and give Coming up's cell its own phosphor (the next day numeral lit).

Keep: the poster type, the readout strip with leaders and the waypoint radar. Fix: restore the parent's section caps in cyan, wheat and lilac on the column heads and the strip, so the page is not monochrome. Show the wordmark on the phone.

a.titles: The best are 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Lit Manual, Relit Rails, carried) and 'Give Vera something to plan.' (desk, quote, manual, departures and settled crosses). Both name who hears the family and the job in one verb, with the lit word at the end. 'Give Vera something to plan.' takes in reminders and wishes as readily as dated plans. 'Tell Vera what needs a plan.' (trued cross) says the job too, but it is longer and the article makes the lit word heavier. 'tell Vera, she'll plan.' (dessau cross) has voice, but it promises that Vera does all the planning, and the lowercase reads as a slogan. The question forms 'What's the plan?' and 'What's our plan?' can be heard as asking the app to show the plan. 'What's on your mind?' (r13-idea-1, r13-mut-3, r13-wild-3) fails: it does not say what FamilyDB is for.

a.notes:
The crosses beat their carried designs in every line on this lens. The big gain is that light came back as INSTRUMENTS that draw the page's own data (the countdown dial, the line from home, the departures clock, the round tubes with day rings, the slot glass), not as washes. That is what the owner's 'reflect more of the page content' and 'bring back the original's effect' both want.

Grafts that worked:
- Lit Manual's countdown dial in Desk Terminal's case (it reads native).
- Desk Terminal's meter in Trued, with a square-root scale.
- Backlit Plate's four-week trace under the Departures board.
- The tour's rail and NOW lamp in Desk Terminal, with the patch lead making the join literal.
- The waypoint rings carrying day numerals on Dessau's radar.
- The quote head in Switchboard (it fits the switchboard ink).

Grafts that read pasted:
- Quote cross's Settled-Light household row, which is the same strip as Settled's.
- Manual's Quote-Board head figure on Plans and Ideas.
- Departures' roundel-plus-cap heads, which repeat what the rail already says.

Camps: the main-camp crosses (Desk, Dessau) are bolder single devices, a cased terminal and a round tube. The tour crosses have richer systems of lit lines (Trued, Departures), and taking the main camp's glass instruments gave them the tubes they lacked. The best next step for the winner is Desk Terminal's case and lead combined with the tour's lit data strips (the line from home, the departures clock) on the inner pages.

Risks: Dessau cross drifts toward monochrome green (88% share), which is the Matrix complaint again. Several crosses leave Home's lower half (Lately added, wishes, setup) completely unlit, so 'light where attention belongs' should give each section one lamp, not none.

scores.why: Has the original light (bloom on the greeting, the lit radar tube, glowing dots), but the green spreads over everything: green-tinted cards, amber washes and pill chips. Inner pages are flat cards with no tube at all. It looks like the Matrix rather than a lit instrument.

The cased terminal is a real green screen, with the lit question typed at the foot of its glass and a block cursor, the strongest 'the machine speaks here' device of the main camp. The desk beside it is calm but a little inert, and inner pages have only a single tube each.

The best soul in the heat. The glass is thinner and truer, 'plan.' is white-hot with the only cursor, and the lit patch lead from the case into Coming up's NOW lamp makes the machine and the desk one drawing. The Plans countdown dial ('NEXT IN 2 DAYS', lit day ticks) and the Status needle are proper 1980s instruments. Light appears only where the machine speaks.

The big condensed heads and the lit 'mind' are confident, and the Next up tube is fine. The numbered keycaps and tracked mono legends read as costume, and below the hero the board is matte with no phosphor of its own.

Calmer and more honest once the costume is gone. 'One live figure per page' (Status's lit 6, Chat's count) is a good scarcity rule, and the setup ring strip gives Home a lit step. The Home tube is still the same small Next up box as before, so the light stays at the hero corner and the board below barely glows.
The huge scanlined 'mind?' and the round radar tube are thrilling. Below the fold the matte poster, navy cards and card-grid To do drop the light entirely.

The round tube is now a real instrument: waypoint rings carry the day numerals, NEXT UP sits on its own band, and every inner page has its own round tube (NEXT IN 2 DAYS, LATE 3, SPENT TODAY). 'plan.' is scanlined with a halo. It risks monochrome (88% green share, every other ink faded to grey), and on the phone the tube falls below the first screen.

The lit greeting board, the breathing lamp at now and the Next up tube as stop one are calm and alive. Inner pages carry their light mostly in rails rather than glass, so Ideas and the month feel under-lit.

The tube is now the line's headlamp, with a lit power wire dropping to its stop. Ideas gains 'THE LINE FROM HOME', a genuine green-screen strip with stations at true drive time. The month has its own glass strip, and Status a moving-coil meter. Glass now appears on every page while the plates stay graphite.
A well-set manual with real tubes (the countdown ring, the radar, the spend ring) and lit NOW rails. Home's tube is small and the figure grid behind Coming up reads as drafting, not phosphor.

The slot glass ('Next in 2 days', bars per weekend, free weekend called out) is a fresh piece of lit data that fills the hero with real phosphor. 'plan.' blooms over a pool, and the Plans countdown ring keeps its NOW trace. The Ideas radar shrank to a dull tile, and the rest of Home is plain bone text with no light.
Vera's line and the dot-matrix board are an evocative station at night. The tinted starter keys (blue, purple) and a small board leave the light faint beyond the box.

The Plans page board is the most CRT-native object in the heat: a scanlined departures screen, a big lit 13:00 clock, dotted leaders and the four-week trace. The lit wire from the box's ring into the board's NEXT UP joins speaker and screen. Home's board is still narrow, and the hover glow and the wire share one green.
The terminal glass holding 'What's the plan?' in VT323 is a pure green-screen prompt, with tubes sized per page. The panels are heavy grey slabs and the radar is small.

'plan.' set alone in VT323 under a three-layer halo with a breathing cursor is the original's soul brought back exactly. Panels lost their grey fill, so the page sits on bare black, and the month has a lit Now edge. The radar is now a tiny scope, Plans names wrap to two lines, and the lit glass is cramped under its own title.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP: the thin cased glass, the lit question with its single cursor, the patch lead into Coming up's NOW lamp, the Plans countdown dial with lit day numerals, and the Status needle with its limit tick. FIX: (1) Home's lower half (kids' wishes, Lately added) has no light at all; give Lately added's NOW-less list a single lit 'newest' lamp, or end the lead's rail in it. (2) The Ideas map's blips overlap at downtown; fan the labels out as Trued's line-from-home does. (3) Move the Ready foot on Settings into the head row so it is not a second header. (4) On the phone, put 'Send where I am' on the FROM row by dropping its label to an icon plus a tooltip.

KEEP: the headlamp tube with its power wire, 'THE LINE FROM HOME' strip on Ideas, the month glass strip, and the square-root spend meter. FIX: (1) The stretched plates on Home leave dead graphite under short names; set them to content height and let the rail ride under them. (2) The Status meter case is too tall; trim it to the banks. (3) On the phone, show the whole Next up tube (or its one-line readout) before the starters, because the light is currently cut off at the fold. (4) Push 'plan.' a little hotter on the board; the halo reads weaker than the desk and settled lines.

KEEP: the Plans departures board (big VT323 clock, dotted leaders, NOW +1W..+4W trace) and the lit wire from the box's ring into NEXT UP. FIX: (1) Home's board is narrow and its clock is tiny; give Home the same big next-departure clock as Plans. (2) Separate the two lights: the row-hover glow should be a steel wash with a sage edge, keeping pure phosphor for the wire. (3) Give the kids' wishes stop a lamp of its own so the branch ends on something. (4) The Ideas radar sits in a small box beside the table; make it the page's header board, as Plans does.

KEEP: the round tube on every page with one live figure, the waypoint rings carrying day numerals, the scanlined 'plan.', and the readout strip of figures. FIX: (1) Bring back a little section ink: the 4px caps are now so faint that the page reads as monochrome green and grey (hue entropy .22). Restore the parent's steel, wheat and heather at about 60%. (2) On the phone, move a small round tube up beside the title rather than below the strip. (3) Every link is underlined, so the page shimmers; underline only on hover and focus. (4) Restore the FamilyDB wordmark on the phone bar.

KEEP: the slot glass of the next four weeks, the lit NOW rails, the hot-cored 'plan.' over its pool, and the Status wiring figure. FIX: the slot glass has dark space above its bars, so print the plan names or day numerals up the bars. Restore the Ideas radar to the parent's size, because it is now a dull tile. Give Lately added and Finish setting up one lamp each.

KEEP: 'plan.' on its own line in VT323 with the halo and cursor, the bare-black panels with one cap, and the quote heads. FIX: (1) Give the glass room: the title squeezes the box. (2) Enlarge the Plans radar back to the parent's scope. (3) Widen the name column so 'Oaks Park roller rink' does not wrap.

KEEP: the de-costumed board, 'one live figure per page' with E1's halo, and the setup ring strip. FIX: the board's three cells have no phosphor. Give Coming up a lit Next numeral or a NOW lamp on its first hop. Make the Home tube draw data, such as the four-week trace or waypoint rings, rather than repeating the stock Next up box.

a.titles: Best through the soul lens: 'Give Vera something to plan.' when it is set ON the glass as the machine's prompt, with 'plan.' white-hot and a single block cursor: Desk Terminal, Patched, and Switchboard, Quoted (where 'plan.' sits alone in VT323). It names the job, names who hears you, and puts the lit word where the eye stops, so it reads like a terminal waiting for input. The same words set in sans on the page (Quote, Manual, Departures crosses) are good but less alive. 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (Lit Manual, carried) is its near-equal and a touch tighter. 'Tell Vera what needs a plan.' (Trued cross) is clear but has a filler 'needs a'. 'tell Vera, / she'll plan.' (Dessau cross) has the most character and suits the poster, but it promises that Vera acts on her own and the comma break is mannered. Weaker: 'What's the plan?' and 'What's our plan?' can be heard as 'show me the plan'. Failing: 'What's on your mind?' (Quote and Dessau carried, today's page), which says nothing of FamilyDB's job and is the line the family heard as generic.

a.notes: Grafts that worked: Desk's patch lead from the terminal to the rail, taken from the tour's line grammar, which is the best cross-camp fusion in the heat. Trued taking Desk's spend meter, redrawn on a square-root scale. Settled's patch-cord quote heads, taken from Quote Board and made native. Departures' four-week trace (from Backlit Plate) under the board. Dessau's readout strip and NOW rail. Grafts that read pasted: Manual's slot glass (an empty bar chart), Quote's Sill Line setup rings (oversized amber circles), and Settled's 'Now' word repeated in the month cell. Comparing the camps: the tour finals bring drawn data (lines, rails, boards) and the main entrants bring identity objects (the terminal, the poster, the figure heads). The best crosses joined the two, a lit object wired to a drawn line (Desk, Departures, Trued). The phosphor light has come back well everywhere. The risk now is convergence: the same title, the same rail with a NOW lamp and the same radar NEXT UP tube appear in nearly every design, so the lines are starting to look alike. Lines should keep their signature. Dessau shows the opposite risk: strong style, but colour drained to green.

scores.why: The original glow has charm, but it is one green wash: every card is the same, there is no hierarchy of light, and the Matrix complaint stands.
The cased terminal beside a matte desk is a real identity with the light kept on the glass. The desk side is neat but plain: list rows under rule heads.
The lit greeting board with its steel branch of starters is lovely, and the track drawing gives the week a shape. The navy-slate plates and the full-width setup band read as stock dashboard.

The lit patch lead from the terminal's socket into Coming up's NOW lamp is the most memorable gesture in the heat: the machine and the desk become one drawing. The thinner case and the bloomed 'plan.' on the glass put the light back where it belongs, and the rest stays grounded slate.
The big condensed figure heads give a confident evening trading-desk mood. The keycap costume and the Alt legend still feel like dressing.

Taking the costume off helps, and the condensed two-line title is handsome typesetting. The lower half is now three equal boxed cards and a five-cell household strip, which reads like a generic dashboard, and the big amber rings in the setup band take more attention than they should.
It has the boldest poster voice, but the navy cards and the matte poster below the fold let it down.

The heat's most distinctive identity: 'tell Vera, she'll plan.' in large lowercase Outfit, a round tube with numbered waypoint rings, and the readout strip of dotted-leader figures. It has become nearly monochrome (88% green share, hue entropy .23), losing the grounded colour the owner asked for, and the inner pages repeat the same poster-plus-badge layout.
A quiet, well-set manual. The Fig. 1 rail grid and the round 'Next in 2 days' tube are charming, but the lower half is plain.

The hot-cored 'plan.' and the rail with its lit NOW are well done. The four-week slot glass reads as an empty bar chart (tall dark glass, thin pillars), so the figure is weaker than the round tube it replaced, and below the fold the page is still bare lists.
Vera's line down the left with interchange keys is a fresh structure. The tinted starter keys (navy, plum) cheapen it.

A genuinely evocative station at night. The dot-matrix departures board with its four-week trace is the most delightful lit object here, and the lit wire from the box's ring into NEXT UP is a lovely, legible device. The matte rails and bone everywhere else make it calm. Its mixed type, with Archivo display set beside Plex, is slightly unsettled.
The videotex map idea is clever and the household index is good. Everything is small and evenly weighted, so it reads as busy.

'plan.' set alone in VT323 under the halo, on the terminal's glass, is the best treatment of the lit word in the heat. The steel patch-cord quote heads are a witty native graft. Small, even-weight panels still crowd the page, and the setup bar across the top steals the opening.

The NEXT UP tube standing on the rail with a power wire, the Ideas 'line from home' at true drive time and the moving-coil spend meter are all lovely, data-true drawings. The graphite plates are calmer than the old navy, but the boxed panels still give it a slightly product-template look.

It has the strongest identity in the field. The cased green terminal at the left of every page, with the lit lead patched into Coming up's rail, makes machine and desk read as one drawing, and each page's tube (the countdown dial on Plans, the radar map on Ideas, late bars on To do, the needle on Status) is drawn from that page's own data, so the companions feel inspired rather than stock. Points come off for the heavy, repeated left column and the long dark tail under the kids' wishes, which make some pages feel more boxed-in than lovely.

The signal-box line language is calm, coherent and has a clear mood: one lamp at now, ring stops, T buffers, the Next up tube standing on the rail, the line from home on Ideas and the spend meter. The Home hero with its lit word 'plan' is warm and inviting. It is a touch more conventional than Desk Terminal: the graphite plates and the forms read closer to a standard dark dashboard, and the tube, being smaller, gives less of a 'that's lovely' moment.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the patch lead, the thin bezel, the bloomed title on the glass and the steel NOW rail. Fix: give the lead a faint afterglow pulse when the tube warms so it reads as live current. Make Lately added's kind rings carry a little grounded section colour (clay, heather, wheat), because the desk is close to colourless now. Balance the short Kids' wishes band under the terminal, perhaps by moving it to the desk or adding Lately's figure there. On To do, the amber hollow rings and the right-aligned dates look heavy; set the dates in tabular sans at a smaller size.

Keep the board, the wire and Vera's line with its stops. Settle the type: set the title in one family, either Archivo condensed or Plex Sans Condensed, not wide Archivo. Separate the board rows' hover glow from the wire's light by using a steel wash on hover. Give the Wishes section real stops, or end the line on a T buffer. Make the board's trace a touch taller and brighter, because it is the page's signature and it reads faint.

Keep the headlamp tube on the rail, the power wire, the Ideas line from home and the Status meter. Fix: on Home's plates, use the spare height with a small drawn element (a kind glyph at size, or a ring stop echo) rather than empty graphite. Fade the outer slate panel boxes to hairline seams so the page reads as one board and not cards. 'Tell Vera what needs a plan.' is long; try 'Tell Vera what to plan.'

Keep the lowercase poster names, the round tube with numbered waypoint rings, the readout strip and the four-shape legend. Fix the monochrome drift: restore the section inks to the 4px caps and the head squares at grounded chroma (sage, clay, heather, wheat), and keep green to the tube, 'plan.' and Send. Vary the inner-page tube by page (a dial on Status, a calendar leaf on Plans) so the poster does not repeat as a badge. Give the month grid's ringed numerals section ink.

Keep the condensed two-line title and the one-live-figure rule. Shrink the setup rings to about 28px with a steel stroke and the amber only on the lamp. Drop the boxed cards for open columns under a 2px section cap, so the board reads as typeset and not as widgets. Give Coming up back a lit figure of its own.

Keep 'plan.' in VT323 on its own line and the patch-cord quote heads. Move Finish setting up below the map, so the glass opens the page. Increase the scale contrast between the two tiers so Plans and To do clearly lead. Give the Plans scope more air.

Go back to the round Next-in tube, or fill the slot glass with something: date labels on every week and the plan names on the pillars. Give the lower sections one figure each (the Fig. device worked in the carried version).

a.titles: Best: Dessau's 'tell Vera, / she'll plan.' It has a voice and makes a promise, and it says the job as cause and effect, with the lit verb landing where the eye stops. It is the only title in the heat with personality. Best setting: Switchboard, Quoted's 'Give Vera something to' over 'plan.' alone in VT323 under the halo, which makes the lit word a typed answer on the glass. 'Give Vera something to plan.' is now on five of the seven crosses. It is clear and inclusive, but the field converging on it costs every design distinctiveness, and in condensed type on two lines (Quote, Departures) the line break before 'to' is weak. 'Tell Vera what needs a plan.' (Trued) is wordy and slightly bureaucratic. 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (the carried Manual) is still the crispest imperative. 'What's the plan?' and 'What's our plan?' (carried) can be read as asking to be shown the plan.

a.notes: Crosses that worked as native features: Desk's rail and NOW taken from the tour (the patch lead makes it one drawing, the best graft in the heat); Trued's moving-coil meter from Desk (redrawn on a square-root scale with a ghost needle, better than the source); Manual's head figure from Quote and the colophon status foot from Desk (both read native in Plex); Quote's household contents-row from Settled and the setup rings (native); Dessau's waypoint rings on the radar and the readout strip (the strip is excellent). Crosses that read pasted: Departures' kind-coloured words on Ideas and its green board hover; Settled's quote cords (ornament at small size); Trued's stretched plates (a layout patch rather than a component). Camps compared: the main camp brings frames (the case, the poster, the board head) that hold every page together. The tour camp brings grammars (rails, stops, NOW, numbered rings) that organise the content inside the frames, which answers the owner's 'changes need to reflect more of the page content'. The best crosses join a main-camp frame to a tour-camp grammar (Desk Patched) or a tour grammar to a main-camp head (Manual Slotted). A standard should take: Manual's hairline-and-rail body, Desk's single cased machine for the lit things, Dessau's leadered figure strip as the head readout, and Trued's or Desk's meter on Status. Dessau's cross regressed on colour (88% green): the light came back, but the grounded inks were lost with it.

scores.why: The original light is all there, but the page has one weight of box, one green and one card grammar for everything. There are no steps in the type and no jobs for the colours, so it reads as a theme rather than a system.

The cased terminal is a strong, repeatable frame that holds on every page. The desk beside it is quieter and less structured than its cross: there is no rail on Coming up and To do is still a flat list.
A clear count-board idea with big condensed figures. The keycap costume, mono legends and boxed cells make it busier than its cross.
A bold poster scale and a round tube, but the hierarchy falls apart below the fold and the rows revert to generic cards, so the system holds only at the top of each page.
The rail grammar with one lit NOW and the manual's figure column are a real system. Some pages carry figures that only decorate (the Home machine drawing), and the head row varies from page to page.
The sommaire and the household index row are good ideas. The type is small and dense, the inner pages' left racks feel cramped, and the page reads tight rather than calm.
Vera's line down the left with stops is a memorable spine. The starters' denim and purple plates and the green-heavy board weaken the colour jobs.
A coherent track language (terminus, ring stops, buffer) with a lit greeting board. Coming up's tube and plates were awkwardly stacked, and the slate bands felt dead in places.

The best-unified drawing in the heat. The patch lead from the case's socket into Coming up's NOW rail ties machine and desk together, and To do now hangs on the same rail with a lit NOW. Every inner page has the same case, tube and deck and an honest data figure (dial, map, late bars, needle). The controls, focus and lamp legend are consistent everywhere.

With the costume off it is a disciplined board: one condensed title plus a figure plus a stacked legend on every page, one lit live figure, and section inks with single jobs. The status contents-lines with lamp rows are the cleanest Status in the heat. The bordered cell boxes everywhere are heavy, and the chat bubbles are still very green.

The leadered figure strip under each poster and the round tubes make a genuinely strong, repeatable head device, and the type scale is the most confident in the heat. But the grounded colour is gone: 88% green share, hue entropy 0.22 and seven guidelines missed. The lowercase page names fight the nav's sentence case. Below the strip the body is generic.

The tube standing on Coming up's rail as the line's head, with the power wire onto its stop, is a fine piece of drawing. The setup line, the To do margin and the month strip all speak the track language, and the Status meter with its lamp banks is excellent. The stretched plates leave empty graphite, and boxes nest three deep on Home (board inside band inside page).

The calmest and most typographic system here: hairline rules instead of boxes, rails with numbered rings on every ordered list (Settings included), the head figure with unit and change on every page, and the highest hue variety with the lowest green share. The slot glass and the 'plan.' glow put light where it belongs. The tall empty slot glass and the one-column form are its weak spots.

The lit wire from the box's stop into the board and the shared departures() board with its four-week trace are a strong, reusable component, and the type tokens are explicit. But the green share has risen to 71% with low hue entropy, the kind words on Ideas are warm stubs that read pasted, and the left line on Home runs past content without carrying much.

The quote head with its cord and the Now device are made native, and the household row is a good index. The type is still small and the page dense. Splitting 'plan.' onto its own VT323 line breaks the sentence's face, and the cords between title and figure read as fiddly ornament at 2.25rem.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP: the case at the left of every page, the patch lead from socket to NOW lamp, rails on Coming up and To do, the inverse NEXT UP, the four-signal legend, and the dial, map, bars and needle tubes. FIX: (1) Home's lower left ends early under the short Kids' wishes. Let Lately added span both tracks, or move Wishes into the case's foot as a one-line row. (2) Ideas map: merge the downtown cluster (6, 8, 10) into one stacked label with a single 44px target that lists the three. (3) Move the folded Ready lip on Settings and the form into the head row so there is one header. (4) Phone: put 'Send where I am' under the field as a toggle row and give FROM, the mic and Send one row. (5) The Plans month grid is plain beside the dial: give plan days the dial's tick numeral style so the two figures share one mark.

KEEP: hairline rules over boxes, the rail grammar everywhere (Settings two-column rails), the head figure with unit and change, the colophon lamp, and the hot-cored 'plan.'. FIX: (1) Home's slot glass is tall and empty above its pulses. Cap it at about 14rem, or add the day labels and plan names as a second row on the glass. (2) Settings two-column: let rows size independently (two separate lists, not a shared grid) so AI model loses its gap. (3) Make the small-caps field eyebrow universal on every form, settings included, at 0.75rem with tracking .06em, for legibility. (4) Raise the Plans NOW trace to 45% with a lamp at both ends so it reads at a glance. (5) Give the idea form a right-hand figure (where it will land, its kind ring) to fill the dead column.

KEEP: the tube as the line's head with the power wire, the setup line, the month strip with one lit run, the Status meter and lamp banks, and the To do date margin. FIX: (1) Let the plates size to their content (align-self: end) with the rail as their floor, and drop the empty graphite; or put a second fact (place or drive time) in the gap. (2) Remove one level of nesting on Home: no band border around Coming up, only the rail as its floor. (3) The title 'needs a' is clunky: use 'Give Vera something to plan.' or 'Tell Vera what to plan.'. (4) Phone: show the whole tube before the bar, or swap it for the one-line Next up readout.

KEEP: the condensed title, figure and stacked legend head on every page, the one lit live figure per page, the Status contents-lines with lamp rows, the household row and the setup rings. FIX: (1) Thin the cell boxes to a hairline with a 2px section cap (as Settled does) so the board is less boxed. (2) Chat bubbles: make the family's lines matte slate and keep the phosphor edge on Vera's newest line only, to bring Chat's green down. (3) Coming up lost its lit numeral: let the next stop's day numeral carry the lamp. (4) Fix the legend's top line to the figure's cap height exactly.

KEEP: the poster head (name plus ink square), the round tube with one figure, and especially the leadered figure strip (TODAY ..... Fri 2 Oct, PLANS ..... 4); that strip is the best head device in the heat and should be a standard for any line. FIX: (1) Bring the grounded section inks back into the body: the kind squares on Lately added and Ideas, the column caps, the family's chat tiles. Green share is 88%, and it should be about 60%. (2) Sentence-case the page names to match the nav, or lowercase the nav as well; pick one. (3) Give the rows below the strip the poster's geometry (the shape column) rather than plain lists. (4) Phone: the radar falls below the first screen, so give it a slim tube readout in the strip.

KEEP: the lit wire from the box's stop to NEXT UP, the shared departures() board with the four-week trace, the --t-* type tokens and the To do segmented key. FIX: (1) Bring the green down: make the board's rows dimmer phosphor and only the next row hot, and stop the whole-row green hover glow (use a steel wash). (2) Ideas kind words: put the colour in the ring only and set the words in --ink-2. (3) The left line on Home should carry stops only where there is content, and end at Setup with a buffer.

KEEP: the household index row, the Now device on lists and the month, the spend meter, and hairline panels with a 2px cap. FIX: (1) Set 'Give Vera something to plan.' on one run in one face, with only 'plan.' lit; splitting the lit word into VT323 on its own line breaks the sentence. (2) Raise the body type a step (rows at 1rem, legends at .8125) and add darkspace between the cells. (3) Shorten or drop the cords in the head titles; a dotted leader does the same job with less ornament. (4) Ideas: fit the kind keys in three rows or use a select.

a.titles: Best: 'Give Vera something to plan.', now the convergent title of five lines. It names who hears you and the job, invites more than dated plans, and puts the lit word last. Manual's setting is the strongest: one line in condensed bone with 'plan.' hot-cored and the full stop in the lit run. Quote's two-line break ('Give Vera something / to plan.') is the best two-line setting, since the lit word gets a line start. Desk's version on the glass also works, with the cursor after 'plan.' giving it the machine's voice. Departures keeps the full stop out of the glow, which is acceptable. Fails: Settled splits 'plan.' onto its own VT323 line, which changes face mid-sentence and stalls the read. Trued's 'Tell Vera what needs a plan.' is grammatical but clunky ('needs a'), and the article sits between the eye and the lit word. Dessau's 'tell Vera, she'll plan.' is punchy and poster-right, but it promises rather than invites, carries the apostrophe, and its lowercase clashes with the rest of the app's sentence case.

a.notes: Every cross improved on its carried design for comprehension, mostly by taking the main camp's head row and figure (quote head) and the tour's rail with one lit NOW. The rail-with-NOW is the most successful graft: it reads naturally in desk, settled, quote and manual. Desk's patch lead is the best of them, because it joins the machine's light to the list it describes, as one drawing. The quote head with figure and unit worked in manual, departures and settled. In settled the steel patch cord between title and figure looks pasted. Departures' lit wire into the board is native to its idea and works. Manual's slot glass (from Backlit Plate) carries real data, but it is oversized for what it holds. Trued's moving-coil meter from Desk Terminal works on Status. Its 'plates stretch to the rail' fix created empty slabs, which hurts the glance. Dessau's cross took the tour's waypoint rings onto a radar with meaningless angles: a figure that looks like data but isn't misleads, which is worse for comprehension than no figure. Dessau also lost its colour range, so sections no longer tell apart. Every design now has 0 targets under 44px on Home (one on quote's phone), against today's 42, and every Tab order is sane except desk and settled, which put tube or setup links before the box. Camps compared: the main crosses (desk, quote) have the clearest one-thing-first Home. The tour crosses (departures, manual, settled) explain more of the service but ask more reading. The two camps have converged: a calm slate page, a title that labels the box, and one lit NOW per list are now shared ground, and the difference between them is in how each draws its figure. Hover afterglow is still nearly invisible in stills for everyone except trued's starter rings and settled's 2px edge.

scores.why: 42 of 55 Home targets under 44px, Next up and the setup card compete with the box at a glance, and the radar/wash read as the same green as every control; the squint gives no clear first thing.

The cased terminal gives the eye one place to start and the deck of keys is generous (0 small targets), but Tab goes through the tube's two links before the box, and the thick case plus a busy desk make the squint a little even.

Title, box, then the steel branch of starters is a clean sight line, and the line with one lit now reads instantly; the tube hung under Coming up's rail is small and the plates in sunk wells take a second read.

The best Home sight line in the heat: lit tube, then the title as the box's label, then the box, with the patch lead carrying the eye into a Coming up rail that reads at a glance (NOW lamp, day, name, time, how long). The faults are small: To do's open rings work as ticks but look like lamps or radios, Tab still reaches the tube's links before the textarea, and the textarea's focus ring is faint.
Its big figures read in the squint, but the costume (keycaps, Alt legend, the 0 gear) and three equal cells with small dense rows make you hunt for the item you came for.

Without the costume this is the calmest board to take in at a glance: a two-line title, the box, the starters, a 44px setup strip with 'Next: choose your own password', then three cells each led by one figure, plus a household row that is a working index. Coming up now starts at plan 2 and has no light of its own, so the next plan is only in the tube; that is a small jump.
The poster title reads first, but 30 small targets, card-style To do and navy cards break the scan below the fold.

Home's poster gives a strong order: title, box, starters, then a base bar of figures that are links (Plans 4, To do 4, Late 3, Ideas 12), and the shape legend in the footer helps. Inner pages fail the glance: on Ideas the list starts below a bare radar and the figure strip, the radar's angles mean nothing on Home, and colour has drifted back to almost all green (88%), so the sections no longer tell apart.
Rails with one lit NOW make every list in time obvious, and its title is the clearest in the field; the Fig. captions and anatomy drawings add reading before you reach the rows.

The title, box and starters are clear, the plans are numbered 1-4 in both the rail and the slot glass (one mark joins the figure to its list), and the glance strip '3 more plans / 4 to do / 3 late' works well. But the tall glass is mostly empty dark, the NOW trace on Plans is easy to miss, and Ideas starts its list low.

Vera's line with the box as its first stop is easy to follow, and the starters' 'usually Plans' lines explain where things go; the board beside the box is small and dim, and the denim and violet starter fills read as selected.

The line down the left, box, starters, Continue and setup reads in order, and the lit wire into a departures board whose rows are whole 44px links is a real gain in understanding. To do doubles each row's mark (an amber rail ring beside a checkbox), the four-week trace under the board is too small to read, and the board's hover glow and the wire use the same green.
The best map of the whole service, with the household index at the foot, but 'What's the plan?' on glass reads as 'show me the plan', and the inner racks put the list in a narrow column.

The most informative Home (every page's figure and its state), and the head row's one green primary is clear on inner pages. But setup sits above the title, so the eye and Tab (four links) hit it before the box; plan names wrap in a narrow column; and the patch cord between label and figure is ornament the eye has to cross.

Title, box and the starter branch make the strongest greeting board, the month strip and the Status meter read at a glance, and the lit run says 'next' without words. The stretched graphite plates leave large empty slabs, the tube's left placement puts Next up apart from the name list, and on the phone only the top of the tube shows.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the title as the box's label inside the glass, the patch lead into Coming up's NOW rail, the two-line starter keys, the Ready foot, and 0 small targets. Fix: (1) Tab order: put the textarea before the tube's 'Oaks Park' and '3 more' links (DOM order or a skip), so a keyboard user lands in the box first. (2) To do: draw the tick as a square box beside the rail stop, not an open circle; a ring reads as a lamp or a radio button. (3) Give the textarea a 2px phosphor focus edge with E4, as the select and Send already have. (4) Even out the lower bench: the kids' wishes band ends about 130px above Lately added, so let it fill or move it into the desk.

Keep: the condensed title with one figure per cell, the 44px setup ring strip with 'Next: choose your own password', the household row as contents lines, and the single 'here' lamp. Fix: give Coming up's first row (the next plan after the tube) a lit day numeral or a NOW tick, so the cell has its own point of light and the eye can tell tube from cell; reconcile Home's Status figure ('1 of 3 lit') with the Status page's ('6 working'); and make Chat's legend say 'today' once chat.py passes a clock.

Keep: Vera's line as the order of Home, the lit wire from the box's ring to NEXT UP, the board rows as whole 44px links, and the 'usually Plans' starter stubs. Fix: on To do, drop the rail ring next to each checkbox (or make the late ring the row's only mark, with the box as the control) so each row has one mark; double the height of the four-week trace and give its numerals 12px or more; change the board's row hover to a steel wash so only the wire is green light.

Keep: the greeting board (title, box, steel starter branch), the lit run from now to the next plan, the month strip and the square-root spend meter. Fix: size the plates to their content, or put the time well under the name, so there is no empty graphite slab; on the phone, show Next up's name and time above the fold (move the tube up or put a one-line readout under the box); and shorten the title to 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (see titles).

Keep: the numbered plans shared by the rail and the slot glass, the 3/4/3 glance strip under the box, and the lit field name on the form. Fix: cut the glass to the pulses' height or add a second line of data (the weekend free, the next title) so it is not dark space; on Ideas, bring the list above the fold by moving the radar card to the side; and make the Plans NOW trace 2px at full phosphor.

Keep: the poster order (title, box, starters, then a base bar of figures that are links) and the footer shape legend, which is the clearest key to state in the heat. Fix: bring back the section inks (green share 88%, hue entropy .23) so Coming up, To do and Ideas tell apart again; put the Home radar's rings back on real bearings or drop the angle and use a straight line of days; and on Ideas set the list beside the radar, not under a bare 15rem tube and strip.

Keep: the service map, the quote heads with figures, the head row's one green primary and the Now rail. Fix: move 'Finish setting up' under the greeting (or into the household row) so the title and box come first for the eye and for Tab; widen the Plans cell's name column so plan names fit on one line; drop the patch cord between label and figure, or shorten it to a dot leader; set 'plan.' inline in the title, not as an orphan VT323 line.

a.titles: The best are "Give Vera something to plan." (desk, quote, departures and manual crosses) and the carried "Tell Vera what to plan." (Lit Manual). Each is an imperative that names who hears you and is the box's own label, so a newcomer knows to type. 'Something' takes in reminders and wishes without saying 'no' to anything. Desk sets it best, inside the glass straight above the box. "Tell Vera what needs a plan." (Trued cross) is clear but runs long: 'needs a' slows the read, and 'a plan' narrows it to one thing. "tell Vera, she'll plan." (Dessau cross) is the punchiest poster line and says what happens next, but its lowercase start and the comma make it read as a slogan, not as the label of the box under it. Switchboard, Quoted puts 'plan.' on its own VT323 line, which splits the sentence, so the eye stops on 'to' and then has to find the verb. The question forms fail this lens: 'What's the plan?' (Settled Light, Trued, Relit) is heard as 'show me the plan', and 'What's our plan?' (Platformed) assumes a plan exists.

a.notes: Every cross improved on its carried design typographically, except settled-cross, which only held level. The best borrowings were type devices. Quote Board's head (a figure in section ink with a stacked unit) worked natively in departures-cross, manual-cross and settled-cross. The main camp's tamed condensed titles went into the tour finals. The tour's rails gave numerals and mono times a column to line up on, which desk-cross and manual-cross used well. Pasted-looking borrowings: settled-cross's VT323 lit word under a sans line; the trued-cross Status meter's VT323 labels in a sans system; and desk-cross's lead line, which is a drawing more than type. Camps: the main-camp crosses (quote-cross, desk-cross, dessau-cross) have the stronger display hierarchy. The tour crosses (manual-cross, trued-cross) have the better body rhythm and figure columns. The standard to aim for is quote-cross's head over manual-cross's rails and body. Recurring faults to fix everywhere: seeded '19:56' times, tracked mono caps used for units and dates, and text below 12px on glass and in margin marks.

scores.why: One undifferentiated sans at small sizes, mono caps for labels, ISO dates and '19:56' on cards. No scale steps between page title, section head and row, and figures don't line up in columns.

The right-aligned time and date columns and the cased glass with VT323 are good. The letterspaced mono phrases ('was due 2 days ago') and the VT323 question at heading size cost legibility and rhythm.
Clean DM Sans and Archivo hierarchy, a margin date column and large rail day numerals. The plates' names are small against their boxes, and the title is set modestly for Home's largest head.
The quote head (a condensed title, a figure in section ink, a stacked unit) is the best page-head device of the main camp. The visible keycaps and the many mono legends add noise.
The heavy 110px lowercase poster is display type that crowds the box, and inner pages fall back to small ISO-dated cards. The type pairing is bold but out of scale.
A coherent Plex superfamily (condensed heads, sans text, mono figures), with the title on one line and the lit word at its end. Figure captions in tiny mono and dense small labels weaken the body.
Calm, well-led rows and a readable 'What's our plan?'. The scale is flat between the section heads and the rows, and the board's dot-matrix is small.
The VT323 title on the glass is less legible, the plan names in the Plans cell wrap to two lines in a narrow measure, and the household index is set in tiny mixed faces.

Real gains: the Plex Sans Condensed title glows on the glass with one hot word, the Coming up rows set a bold day numeral and a sans month against a mono time column that lines up, and To do's dates are right-aligned two-line marginalia over amber 'was due'. The letterspaced-mono problem is fixed; only VERA · FRI 2 OCT and FROM stay in tracked caps.

The strongest type SYSTEM in the heat. Every page opens on a condensed Archivo title, a light figure in section ink and a stacked unit, and the board heads carry the figure on the label's baseline over a dotted leader. The hop rows' big day numerals set the week's rhythm. It loses a little to the seeded '19:56' times and '#4' ids on To do, to tight 600-weight condensed row titles, and to tracked mono caps in the units.

Typographically the most 'set' page in the heat: a tamed 90px Outfit poster, light 01/02/03 folios on Status, uppercase underlined labels with leaders to right-aligned tabular figures, and ringed day numerals in the month grid. Against it: lowercase page names ('status', 'plans') fight sentence case, the type around the green is all one colour (green share 88%), and the phone hides the wordmark.

The Plex superfamily is used with clear jobs: 'Give Vera something to plan.' on one line with the lit word last, mono date and time columns that line up on the rail, a small-caps figure row (3 MORE PLANS / 4 TO DO / 3 LATE) and well-led To do rows with amber due words. The slot glass's numerals are small, and the setup and Lately added tables run very wide.

Archivo 700 at 88% width with balanced wrapping is a handsome title, the plates' names and the mono time wells are nicely contrasted, and the rail's light day numerals with tiny 'Oct Sun' stacks read like a timetable. The plates leave dead space under short names, and the stacked 'Sep/Sun' margin marks are near the floor of legibility.

The Archivo title is confident, the VT323 board rows are well set with dotted leaders and a right-aligned date column, and every head has a roundel and a figure. The title is large for the column, the body copy in the board is small, and the footer drops to tiny grey sans.

The quote heads with cords are a neat idea, but the title splits faces ('Give Vera something to' in condensed sans, 'plan.' in VT323 on its own line), so the key word looks smaller and orphaned. Plan names wrap to two lines in a cramped measure, and the units are letterspaced mono ('of 3 on').

fixes.suggestion: Keep the quote head (condensed title, figure in section ink, stacked unit over change) as the app's page-head standard, and keep the hop rows with large day numerals. Fix To do: drop the '#4' ids from the title column (or set them as faint tabular figures in their own column), and show the hour only when one was set ('was due Sun 27 Sep', not '19:56'). Set the row titles in regular-width sans 500 instead of condensed 600, which is too tight at 1.125rem. Set the stacked units in sentence-case sans 0.8125rem rather than tracked mono caps, so mono is kept for figures in columns. On Home, give Coming up's cell back one lit numeral (the next stop) so the board has phosphor of its own.

Keep the one-line Plex Sans Condensed title with 'plan.' hot at the end, the mono date and time columns on the rail, and the small-caps figure row under the box. Raise the slot glass's numerals to at least 1.25rem with the next one hot, and fill or shorten the empty glass above the pulses. Cap the setup steps and Lately added at about a 46rem measure instead of the full width. Make the small-caps eyebrow the rule for every form label, settings included, at 0.75rem with +0.06em tracking.

Keep the condensed title on the glass with its bloom and the one hot word, the right-aligned two-line To do dates, and the bold sans day numeral beside the mono time column. Set the day numerals in Coming up tabular so '4' and '17' align on their right edge. Replace the tracked 'VERA · FRI 2 OCT' and 'FROM' caps with sentence-case sans small. Pull the Lately added '#1-#4' into faint tabular figures, or drop them.

Keep the Archivo 700 at 88% title with text-wrap: balance, the graphite plates with mono time wells, and the rail's light day numerals. Shorten the plates to their content (or set the name at about 24px so it fills the plate) to remove the dead graphite. Raise the margin's stacked 'Sep/Sun' to 12px minimum, or set it as one line ('Sun 27 Sep'). The 'now' word on the To do rail would read better in sentence-case sans than in green mono.

Keep the 01/02/03 light folios, the uppercase underlined labels with leaders to tabular figures, the ringed day numerals in the month grid and the tamed poster scale. Capitalise the page names ('Status', 'Plans'), or keep the lowercase only for Home's poster, so the inner pages read as titles. Restore the wordmark on the phone. Bring a second, grounded ink into the strip's figures and labels so the type is not all green-on-black (green share 88%).

Keep the VT323 board rows with dotted leaders and the right-aligned date column, the roundel heads and the four-week trace. Step the title down to about 2.25rem so it fits the column without a two-line bulk, raise the board's foot labels (NOW +1W...) to 12px, and set the footer copyright at the body's small step rather than a smaller grey.

Keep the quote head with its cord, and the household index. Set the whole title in one face (condensed bone with 'plan.' lit in the same face), or move the VT323 to a prompt line over the box, so the key word is not smaller and orphaned. Widen the Plans list's title column, or shorten the time column, so 'Oaks Park roller rink' sits on one line. Set the units in sans, not letterspaced mono.

a.titles: The best is 'Give Vera something to plan.', in manual-cross's setting: one line, the lit word and the full stop last, and the sentence says the app's job. Quote-cross's break before 'to' ('Give Vera something / to plan.') is the best two-line setting and the most poster-like. Desk-cross sets the same words well on the glass. Departures-cross breaks the same way, but at too large a size for its column. Settled-cross fails on setting, not wording: it moves 'plan.' to its own line in another face (VT323), so the key word reads smaller and detached. 'Tell Vera what needs a plan.' (trued-cross) is longer, and 'a plan' sounds a little bureaucratic. 'tell Vera, she'll plan.' (dessau-cross) is punchy and suits a poster, but its lowercase start and two clauses make it a slogan, not a label for the box. The yardsticks' questions ('What's the plan?', 'What's on your mind?') can be heard as 'show me the plan' or as vague; the imperative is clearer.

a.notes: The crosses beat their carried parents in usability on every line except desk, where the patched-in rail-stop ticks cost the most basic To do task. Grafts that worked: Quote Board's head figure with a change link, taken by settled, manual, departures and dessau, gives every page a 'how many, how late' answer that is also a filter link. The lit NOW divider on To do (everyone) shows what is overdue at a glance. Sill Line's setup ring strip (quote, trued, desk) makes the next step one obvious link. Settled's household row, borrowed into quote, puts status at a glance. Dessau's readout strip of linked figures works. Grafts that read pasted or cost usability: desk's rail-stop controls (a tick that looks like a lamp); departures' ring stops on form fields (they look like radios); manual's slot glass (a figure that doesn't name what it counts); dessau's re-seated radar bearings (angle with no meaning); and settled's VT323 'plan.' orphaned on its own line. The camps compare like this: tour finals were already the more effortless on Home (box first, starters that say where they land, margin dates). Main-camp grafts gave them stronger page heads, so the tour crosses lead this heat (trued, settled). The main camp's best usability gain came from shedding costume (quote) and from Dessau's surprisingly good To do. All crosses but dessau (Plans 6, chat-phone 2) hold 0 small targets on the main pages, and minimum text is 12-13px everywhere. The low points for tired eyes are the VT323 board rows and green-on-black dot text at small sizes.

scores.why: Plain and familiar, but 42 targets under 44px on Home (46 on To do), To do as cards with ISO dates, and no late filter or late signal at a glance. Working out what is overdue takes reading every card.

The terminal column holds the filters, the status and the question in one predictable place, and there are 0 small targets. The digit-keycap, letterspaced-mono habit and the terminal-as-sidebar on every page add a second place to look before the list.

The title is the box's label, the starters say where each lands, and To do has margin dates with a lit now. The Next up tube hangs under the rail and on the phone sits below the fold, so 'what is this weekend' takes a scroll.

Home is very clear: the question, the box and the starters in one case, Coming up as one dotted table, and the setup strip. But on To do, and in Home's To do, the tick is now a round amber ring on the rail. A first-timer reads it as a 'late' lamp, not a box to tap, which breaks 'tick off a to-do'. There is also no Home key in the bar.
The count board reads at a glance, but the visible digit keycaps and the 0 gear are costume a family member must learn to ignore, and the To do and filter rows are dense.

Taking the costume off paid. Home is the box, three equal cells with feet on one line, a setup ring strip and a household row, so every task has an obvious door. To do has a latched key row with 'Late 3' in amber, and Ideas has one row of kind keys, so 'show only the restaurants' is one click.
Huge poster title, 30 targets under 44 on Home and 37 on To do, To do back in cards with ISO dates. Hard work for tired eyes on a phone.

The best To do page in the heat: a 'Tick when done' column head, real Edit buttons, a readout of Open 4 / Late 3 / No date 1 whose figures are links, and a lit NOW. But page names are lowercase posters, Home's radar angle means nothing, Plans has 6 small targets, and the kind colours sit only dE 8.6 apart (4.3 for deuteranopes), which hurts finding the restaurants by colour.
The rails with one lit NOW are easy to read. The figure column on many pages pushes the list right and adds a picture to decode before acting.

Home is clear: the title, a full-width box, starters, and a strip of 3 more plans / 4 to do / 3 late as links, then a numbered Coming up rail. Ideas has a chip row with counts per kind. The tall slot glass says 'Next in 2 days' without naming the plan, and most of its height is empty dark.
The box comes first in a left line with starters that name their destination. The departures board is readable, though the coloured starter fills and the rail rings everywhere add noise.

Home is good: the board names Next up and the three after it with dates, and on the phone the lit wire leads straight from the box to the board. But the new-idea form now hangs empty ring stops beside every field, which read as radio buttons a first-timer will try to click. The VT323 board rows at 1.2rem are the hardest text to read on a phone at night.
A map of every page from Home, with good sized type. The Plans rack and Ideas' wrapping kind keys bury the filter, and Home has 1 small target.

Home answers almost every family task at a glance. Setup is the first line, the box is lit, Plans and To do each have a quote figure with a lit Now, and Ideas and the household row (Wishes, Memory, Family, Status with Telegram off and Calendar off, Settings) are all links. There are 0 small targets and the smallest text is 13px. On Ideas the kind keys still wrap to 4 rows with More filters at the fold, and the VT323 'plan.' alone on its own line reads like a broken title.

The most effortless Home. The title is the box's label, the starters say 'usually lands in Plans / To do / Ideas', the Next up tube names the plan beside plates with time wells, and setup is one strip. To do is clean, with margin dates, a lit now and Edit links. The phone shows only the top of the tube above the tab bar, and short plate names leave empty graphite.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the title as the box label, the starters with their 'lands in' line, the stop-one tube and the setup strip. On the phone, put the tube's name and time (NEXT UP, Oaks Park, 13:00 in 2 days) above the starters, or fold the starters to one row, so 'what's on this weekend' is on the first screen. Shorten plates to their content height, or put who it is for and the time under the name, to remove the empty graphite. On To do, add a 'Late 3' key beside Open, as quote-cross and dessau-cross do, rather than only the head link.

Keep the setup line first, the quote heads with a lit Now, and the household row with status lamps. That row is the best 'is everything working?' answer in the heat. Set 'Give Vera something to plan.' on one or two lines in a single face, keeping the lit 'plan.' in VT323 at the end of the line, not orphaned on its own. On Ideas, make the kind keys a single scrolling row or a select with a 'Restaurants' shortcut, and lift More filters above the fold.

Keep the uncostumed board, the three equal cells, the latched To do keys with Late in amber and the Ideas kind key row. Home's Status cell says '1 of 3 lit' while Status says '6 working': use one count. Give Coming up's cell back a lit Next numeral, or start it with Next up, so it does not look like the plans start on the 9th. The chat legend should say 'today' only when true, and the new-idea form's '+1' figure is ornament: drop it.

Keep the full-width box, the 3/4/3 link strip and the numbered Coming up rail. Make the slot glass name the next plan ('Oaks Park roller rink, Sun 13:00') under 'Next in 2 days', and cut its height to the pulses, which halves the empty dark. Make the Remind me starter's resting state match its siblings: it shows as selected in the still.

Keep Home's one case (question, box, starters, Ready foot) and Coming up as one dotted table. Undo the round-ring ticks on To do: put the square checkbox back and let the ring on the rail stay a lamp, amber for late. 'One control, one look' is the rule this breaks. Add a Home key to the bar, and on the phone move 'Send where I am' to the same row as From by shortening it to an icon with a visible label underneath.

Keep the To do page as the model for every crossing: the 'Tick when done' head, the Edit buttons, the readout strip whose figures filter, and the lit NOW. Set page names in sentence case, not lowercase, and bring them to 56-64px. Give Home's radar real meaning or replace it with a plain Next up plate. Fix Plans' 6 small targets (the month's day rings), and split the kind colours further apart, or add the kind's icon, so restaurants are found without colour. Restore the FamilyDB wordmark on the phone.

Keep the board as Home's and Plans' Next up, and the phone's wire from the box down to the board. Take the ring stops off the form's fields: they read as radio buttons, so keep only the final lit stop at Add it. Set the board rows in Plex Mono, or VT323 at 1.4rem or more, on the phone. Give Wishes' end on Home a stop or a link row so the line does not just stop.

a.titles: "Give Vera something to plan." (desk, quote, manual, departures, settled) says FamilyDB's job best through a usability lens: an imperative that names who hears you, takes in reminders and ideas as well as dated plans, and works as the box's label, so a newcomer knows to type there. Best settings: quote-cross and departures-cross (two lines, 'plan.' lit at the end) and manual-cross (one line). Settled-cross splits it badly, with 'plan.' alone on a line in a different face, which reads as a broken title. Desk-cross sets it below the Next up block inside the glass, so it is the second thing read rather than the first. "Tell Vera what needs a plan." (trued-cross) is clear and labels the box well, but 'needs a plan' is a little heavier and suggests only things needing planning. It is still second best, close to the carried "Tell Vera what to plan." (manual's parent). "tell Vera, she'll plan." (dessau-cross) is a slogan, not a label: lowercase, a comma splice, and it promises an outcome rather than saying where to type. The question titles on the carried designs ("What's our/the plan?", "What's on your mind?") can be heard as 'show me the plan', the opposite of the box's job.

scores.why: The baseline the owner rejected: it is green everywhere, about 82% of the colour on the page, with glowing cards and no grounded colour. The light is real, but it lights everything, so nothing stands out. It reads as the Matrix.
A strong cased terminal, but VT323 still breaks the apostrophe in 'What's on your mind?'. The amber-outlined checkboxes on Home's To do read as warnings, and the thick case is costume weight.

Clear count heads, but the digit keycaps and the Alt legend make it look like dressing up, and the steel latched nav block is the loudest thing in the bar. The ambient wash behind the board turns muddy.
The poster scale has real spark, but the 110px lowercase title is costume. Below the fold it is navy-ish cards, To do falls back to cards with ISO dates, and 30 targets on Home are under 44px.
Honest rails with one lit NOW, but the manual's 'Fig. 1' captions and the glowing round gauges feel academic. Below the greeting the page is flat and long.
A dense, coherent map of the service, but the racks are cramped. The VT323 'What's the plan?' on glass is a costume prompt, and Chat's filled green Send pushes its green share up.
Vera's line down the left is a real structure. The starter keys are tinted plum and teal fills, which the lessons have already failed, and the board's green is a bit loud beside the box.
A coherent signal-box system with grounded plates, but the Next up tube sits shrunken inside the plates and the month is overlaid with rails. 'What's the plan?' can be heard as 'show me the plan'.

A real improvement. The condensed-sans title on the glass fixes the broken apostrophe, the lit lead from the case into Coming up's NOW lamp ties the machine to the desk, and the Plans dial now carries day numerals. Against it: To do's ticks are now amber rings that look exactly like lamps, so the control you press reads as a state (one control, one look is broken). The steel-blue latched key is a cold slab, and the kids' wishes stub leaves a dead hole at lower left.

The costume is gone, and the setup rings and household index row work. But the amber-outlined checkboxes and the wheat-amber To do '4' sit beside amber 'was due', so half the board reads as a warning. Every plan title is underlined, the green pool under the greeting spills onto Lately added as a muddy wash, and its home is close to Settled's quote cells.

The biggest jump in the heat. Poster type at a sane 90px, the half-dial with waypoint numerals and the TODAY/PLANS/TO DO/LATE/IDEAS readout strip make Home read at a glance. Against it: 88% of its colour is green (hue entropy .225) despite the pastel caps, every row title is underlined, amber triangles are scattered across the page, seven guidelines are missed, the kinds are only dE 8.6 apart, and the lowercase 'tell' is still a costume.

The most complete system here. The tube stands full height as the line's lit head, with its power wire to the stop, and a lit run goes from now to the next plan only. The plates are graphite, the setup line is one band, the month has its lit strip, and Status gets a square-root meter. Against it: short-named plates leave empty graphite, a leftover hover lights one plate in the still, 'what needs a plan' is a clumsy article, and on the phone the tube is pushed below the fold.

Quiet and well set, with rails everywhere and a lit field label on the form. But the 'slot' glass reads as an empty equaliser: four thin bars in a tall black well, with 'Next in 2 days' unanchored. The page below the welcome plate is flat and loses the phosphor, and the 'Remind me to…' starter looks latched in the still.

The wire from the box's ring into the board's NEXT UP is the best cross-camp feature in the heat: it says that what you type becomes a departure. The board's four-week trace and the right column hanging from its own branch are real structure. Against it: the warm kind words (Restaurant in orange) push other_colour_neon to 15.7, the green share rose to 71%, and the board's hover and the wire share one green.

The household index along the foot and the setup line at the top are useful. But 'plan.' alone on a second line in VT323 looks like a broken wrap, not a lit word. The Plans cell squeezes names onto two lines beside the radar, and the quote heads' little steel cords are ornament that the eye has to step over.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the full-height tube with its power wire, the run lit from now to next only, the graphite plates, the one-band setup line, the month's glass strip and the square-root meter. Fix Home: stop stretching the plates to the rail, and instead give each plate a two-line foot (kind, then who and time) so short names leave no empty graphite. Make sure no hover state survives into the still. Phone: bring NEXT UP's name and time above the fold by shrinking the tube to 60% width beside the head. Change the title to 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (drop 'needs a').

Keep the condensed-sans title on the glass, the patch lead into NOW, the 6px case and the Plans dial with day numerals. Fix To do (Home and page): put the square tick box back as the control, and keep the amber ring only as the stop lamp beside it, because a ring you press is indistinguishable from a lamp. Replace the steel-blue latched slab (nav To do, Open) with a graphite key with a phosphor LED and an underline. Close the lower-left hole by moving the kids' wishes up into the case's foot as one line, or by setting it beside Lately added.

Keep the wire from the box's ring to NEXT UP, the board with the four-week trace, and the branch through the section roundels. Fix: set Lately added's kind words in --ink-2 with only the ring in kind colour (the orange 'Restaurant' is the neon outlier). Give the board's row hover a steel wash rather than green, so the only green line is the wire. Trim the board's green fill so its share drops back toward 60%.

Keep the 90px poster title, the half-dial with waypoint numerals, and the readout strip (the best at-a-glance device in the heat). Fix: take the underlines off every row title (underline on hover and focus only). Cut the amber triangles to the LATE cell and the late rows only. Set the title in sentence case ('Tell Vera, she'll plan.'). Give the kinds hues further apart than the ash rose and lilac pair, and put a little grounded colour into the body (wheat figures, clay family) so the page is not 88% green.

Keep the rails, the colophon and the lit field label. Rework the slot glass: put the four plan days as labelled bars with the plan's name beside the tallest, or shrink the glass to the welcome plate's height, so it is not an empty equaliser. Carry one live light below the fold (the NOW lamp at Coming up).

Keep the household index row and the top setup line. Set the title on one line, or break it as 'Give Vera / something to plan.' in one face, so 'plan.' never stands alone in VT323. Widen the Plans cell or drop the radar to a smaller scope so the names stay on one line. Drop the steel cord ornaments from the quote heads.

Keep the setup rings strip and the household contents row. Make the checkboxes steel, never amber, and set To do's figure in bone so amber means late only. Remove the underlines from plan titles, and confine the greeting's green pool to its plate so it does not wash Lately added.

a.titles: The best is 'Tell Vera what to plan.' (the carried Lit Manual title): it names who hears you and the one job in one verb, it fits one line, and the lit word comes at the end. Second is 'Give Vera something to plan.' as manual-cross sets it, on one line with the full stop lit. It is honest and broad, but four of the seven crosses converged on it word for word, which is a near-duplicate warning for the field. In two lines (quote, departures) 'something' carries no weight, and settled's VT323 'plan.' stranded on its own line reads as a wrap bug. 'Tell Vera what needs a plan.' (trued-cross) fails on the stray article. 'tell Vera, she'll plan.' (dessau) is the punchiest and makes a promise, but the lowercase is costume and it adds an apostrophe. 'What's our plan?' and 'What's the plan?' can still be heard as 'show me the plan'.

b.notes: Through the owner's lens, the tour camp's crosses gained the most. Waypoint and Sill took the main camp's structure (rule heads, the one-machine foot, head rows, a type system) and became complete, calm systems without losing their lines. Those borrowings read native, not pasted. The main camp's crosses gained most from the tour's line art and instruments. Listing's lit stem (from Sill Line) is the standout borrowing and worth spreading. Folio's NOW rails and its radar's day numerals sit naturally in the contents grammar. Plate's day numeral (from Waypoint) and lamp strip (from Trued) work, but its destination-legend starters with coloured edges read pasted, and violet is off-period. Pocket's Status meter and ledger (from the main camp) work well. Its Home cards were left boxed beside the line and read unintegrated. On glow: every cross restored real halo on the key word and the tubes. Waypoint's pool and Sill's NOW run are the best-judged 'light where attention belongs'. Folio's halo'd 'on' inside the glass and its listening status line are the most CRT-souled greeting. On colour: all keep grounded slate, steel and bone with amber for late. Waypoint's warm bone leads come closest to brown, which the owner disliked, but they are thin and support the green. Folio's ochre serif figures lean warm too. Measured green share is lowest on Waypoint (43%) and Folio (50%). Plate (69%) and Sill (62%) are still green-heavy, mostly from the glass. On visible change across the page content, Waypoint, Folio and Sill change every page. Plate and Listing still look like their parents below the greeting. Against the anchors, Waypoint, Ruled edges Trued, Relit for this lens, Sill, Squared draws level with it, and every cross beats Desk Terminal, Joined.

scores.why: The most complete system here. The route's arcs carry the day numerals in rings, the same 300-weight numeral leads each row, and a ruled readout strip is lit only at Today and Late. The rule heads are engraved and the shape law is keyed in the footer. Glow sits on 'plan.', the Next leg, the tube and Ready, and the rest is grounded bone, slate and amber edges. Every page changes: Plans' month route, the Status needle tube, To do's amber row edges and Whose filter.

The owner's line language on every page: the steel branch of starters with a junction ring, the sill rail lit only from now to stop one, the chat track ending in 'your turn', and the legend track in the footer. Status's glass lamp board and meter put the CRT back into the page where it belongs. It loses a little because the plates float above the rail with the numerals below it, so plate and stop read as two things, and the boxed To do and Lately added panels are plainer than the top of the page.

Still the strongest drawing of the track idea, with the plates hung from the Coming up line and the stepped setup track. Status's lamp strip on glass and its afterglow are very much on motif. The rail through every week of the month is the one excess.

The greatest typographic variety in the heat: Fraunces page titles and figures, Plex small caps, page numbers and contents leaders. The radar carries day numerals beside a NOW rail, and the household's contents index finally balances the columns. It is a rich, magazine-like page with real halo on 'on' and the tubes. The serif pulls a little toward an almanac and away from the terminal, and the boxed cells still read as a dashboard.

One steel line of time with rings, a lit Now lamp and a breathing Next ring runs down every page. Vera's lines glow while the family's stay matte, which is a fine light rule. The Status meter and its ledger are good, and the diary-set dates give real typographic charm. Home's right column is still three boxed cards beside the line, and there is dead ground under them.
