The bold Home with the lit wire from the tube onto the rail, and Status's lamp board on glass are strong on motif. The 'planning' glow block is heavy, and the inner pages are plainer.
The waypoint arcs and readout strip were already lovely. The boxed bays and inverted Today chip are what the cross fixed.

The lit stem from Next up's tube down to the NOW lamp is exactly the line that draws the eye through the frame, which the owner prizes. The Plans dial and the Status cost dial add CRT instruments to inner pages. The head column gives every page one left edge. The rows sit in filled slate strips that feel heavy, the head-column tiles float as small orphan icons, and much of the page is still a plain listing.

A clear improvement on its parent. The new title and the scope slot carry day numerals, the Status lamp strip and joined spend and trace glass are good, and the engraved seams calm the page. The violet-edged starter keys are off-period, the 'leak' under 'plan' reads as a stray dash, and the lists themselves are much the same generic rows.
Bold and varied, with page numbers, serif numerals and green glass. It is busy, and it is boxed everywhere.
A clean head-column listing with a small NOW rail. The plain 'What's on your mind?' title stays, and there is little line art or light beyond the tube.
Desk Terminal is a well-made console with good CRT glass. The page reads as numbered boxed panels with little line art, and its title is still 'What's on your mind?'.
Calm rule heads and good glass, but it keeps 'What's on your mind?' and has hardly any lines that draw the structure.
Today's page: the original glow, but it is too bright and nearly all green, and the layout is boxy.

It is nearly the same design as Pocket Diary, Lit: a calm slate page with the steel line-of-time art the owner likes, green light only where something is now or live, and a little grounded colour in the muted kind wells and the amber late marks. It scores just below its cross because the dashed Now rules, the boxy square nodes and the plainer Status ledger make it a bit flatter and more monochrome. The cross brings in more varied, material colour without adding more glow.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the route arcs with ringed numerals, the readout strip, the rule heads with bone leads, the amber row edges with triangles, the pool under 'plan.', and the month route that draws each waypoint once. Fix Home's empty right column beside Coming up: hang the Google note from the route's end tick as a caption, or move the Next tube's 'Ready' line there, so the band does not end in about 150px of ground. Add a short vertical track to To do with NOW as a lit node (it is half there now), so the line language reaches the lists. Put the faint scanline mask on the readout strip's lit cells too. On Ideas, keep the kind keys to one row: fold Seasonal and Show into 'More' or let the row scroll inside a fixed rack.

Keep: the branch of starters with its junction ring, the sill rail lit only from now to stop one, the T buffer, the legend track in the footer, the chat track, and Status's lamp board and meter on glass. Fix the plates: set the day numerals above the rail at each plate's foot, or join each plate to its ring with a visible leg, so plate, ring and date read as one stop. Unbox To do and Lately added into rule-headed lists hung from short tracks, so the lower half matches the top's craft. Restore 'Day' on To do's page for consistency, or drop it on Home. Let the Next tube touch the rail with a lit drop, as in Ticked, rather than resting above it.

Keep: the Fraunces titles and figures, the page numbers, the contents leaders, the radar with day numerals beside the NOW rail, the household index in the right column, and the tally tube on To do. Fix: change 'What's on for us?' to a title that asks the family to hand something over, since it reads as asking the app to show what's on. Pull the cells' top borders back to hairlines so the dashboard boxing recedes, and let the rails do the grouping. Give Ideas a rail too (its leaders already work). Bring a little more VT323 or terminal type into the page heads so the serif almanac stays a terminal's magazine.

Keep: the line of time with rings, the lit Now lamp and breathing Next, the glowing Vera lines and matte family lines, the diary-set dates, and the Status meter with its ledger. Fix: unbox the right column on Home (To do, wishes, something to eat) and hang it from its own short line with ring nodes, as the left side does. Fill or shorten the ground under it. Raise Coming up above the fold on the phone by moving the Next tube under Coming up's head. Rename 'Later / Lately added'.

Keep the lit stem from the tube to NOW. It is the best single line in the heat: let it continue faintly down to To do's NOW, so one lit thread ties the evening together. Keep the round dials on Plans and Status. Fix: lighten the filled slate row strips into hairline-led rows so the stem and leaders carry the page. Give the head-column tiles a ring or rail joining them to their band head, so they no longer float. Consider 'Tell Vera what to plan.' in place of 'line up', since two lit words make a long glow block.

Keep: the scope slot with day numerals, the overlapping round radar window, the joined spend and trace glass with its lamp strip, and the engraved seams. Fix: replace the violet and ochre starter edges with one steel edge and section labels in text colour. Remove the leak dash under 'plan.' or make it a clear pool. Draw a thin track down To do with NOW as a lit node, and let the slot's tick marks drop onto the Coming up rows as a rail, so the plate's lines reach the lists.

b.titles: "Give Vera something to plan." (waypoint-cross and plate-cross) says the job best. It names who hears you and what she does, invites handing anything over, cannot be answered 'no', and its single short lit word ends the line. On the waypoint cross, with the pool under 'plan.', it is the strongest greeting here. "What needs a plan?" (sill-cross) is a close second: it is open to reminders and wishes, and the short lit 'plan' is a real improvement on Ticked's heavy 'planning'. "What can we pencil in?" (pocket-cross) is warm and in the family's own voice, and the diary metaphor fits. But 'pencil' is six lit letters and suggests only tentative entries, not reminders or ideas. "Tell Vera what to line up." (listing-cross) is close to the favoured 'what to plan', but 'line up' is an idiom, and two lit words make a long glow block. "What's on for us?" (folio-cross) fails the job test: it asks the app to show what is on, the opposite of the box's purpose. The carried "What's on your mind?" (Backlit Plate, Evening Listing, Folio Switchboard) fails outright as a generic chat opener the owner rejected.

b.notes: The crosses that worked took a light device and used it to bring the tube's light down into the page's content. Listing-cross's stem from the tube to NOW, taken from Sill, is the best transplant: it answers the owner's 'reflect the page content'. Folio-cross's NOW rails with the unboxed radar beside them, taken from the track and Waypoint lines, are a close second. The status line on the glass makes the tube a terminal again. Taken features that read pasted: the plate's placards ('PLANS · RINGS 1·2·4 WK') are fussy for what they say. Sill-cross's square-tick and rule-head tidying made it more correct but less lit than its parent. Waypoint's shape key in the footer is a nice system device, but it sits as a caption. As for the two camps: the main-camp crosses gained the most by borrowing the tour's lit lines (the stem, NOW rails), while the tour crosses gained structure from the main camp (rule heads, readout strips) and lost a little glow on the greeting. The best of each restores light on the question itself (folio's glass, plate's stencil, listing's halo), which is what the owner asked to bring back.

scores.why: All soul and no restraint: the tube, the halos and the green type are everywhere, so the light means nothing in particular and the page reads as the Matrix. It is the reference for the light the others should keep, not a page to keep.
The question is typed on the tube under Next up, with a cursor, so the screen is something you talk to. Glow is scarce and the Ready foot is a live light. The lower page is calm but plain.

The lit wire from now to the tube's stop is real phosphor doing a job, and the Status lamp bank glows meaningfully. The greeting box is a plain slate card, so Home's first read is less lit than the main leader's.
The big Next up tube with its radar is a real monitor and the bloom is kept to the screen. Everything else is flat slate, so the plate idea is not yet visible as an object.

The stencil 'plan.' at full tube strength, the round radar cut overlapping the screen and the scanlined slot glass give the original light back where it belongs. The plate stays matte. The leak cut under 'plan' reads as a stray dash or an underline, and the green share stays high.
Bands and a head column are well structured, and the tube's bar trace is a nice live drawing. But the light stops at the tube, so the listing below is lifeless slate.

The white-cored stem drops from Next up's tube, turns along Coming up's rule and lands on NOW. That is the clearest gesture in the heat of the tube's light reaching the page content. The 'line up.' halo and the tube's bars are alive, and the bands below stay grounded. The stem's long horizontal run across the empty gap is a little heavy.

Of the carried designs this is the most CRT-native: a big radar tube with the question on the glass in VT323 and teletext page numbers. The green cells and boxes crowd the page, though, and the glow is spread wide.

The question sits on scanlined glass with only 'on' haloed, and a VT323 status line with a blinking cursor runs under the field ('4 plans · 3 late · Vera is listening'). The tube is alive and says a fact. The unboxed radar beside the NOW rail and the lit NOW line on To do keep phosphor where the machine is, and the graphite and Fraunces are grounded everywhere else. Under the Fraunces head the 'What's on' greeting is a bit dim.
'planning' lit as the board's headline, with the tube's lit wire dropping onto the Coming up rail, is strong phosphor storytelling. The green-edged board and starters push the green share up.

The lit run from now to stop one, the plates standing on the rail and the needle meter inside Status's glass are lit with meaning. The greeting box is now plain slate, and the tube is smaller and sunk below the box, so Home's first screen is less alive than Ticked's.
The tube with its warm-up bars and the Now lamp on the steel line are good. The greeting is lit only faintly, and much of the page is matte rows.

The lit Now lamp, the breathing Next ring and the 'pencil' halo in a box lit from below bring life back. The tube with its warm-up trace is a real monitor. The right column's sticky shelf leaves dead dark below it, and the line's rings are many and small.
The waypoint arcs and the lit leg are a fresh instrument, and the tube is real. The yellow-bordered setup strip and the readout row feel more dashboard than tube.

The pool under 'plan.', the lit arc from Now to the Next ring and the readout strip with a breathing Today give alive, exact light, and the tube carries a Ready chin plate. Its tube is small and sits to one side, and the 150px of empty ground beside Coming up weakens the cockpit.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the scanlined glass greeting with the haloed 'on', the VT323 status line with its cursor, the unboxed radar beside the NOW rail, the contents lines and the graphite. Fix: lift the Fraunces greeting's off-word ink so 'What's ... for us?' reads as bone on glass rather than dim. Put the blinking cursor at the end of the prompt line as well, so the field reads as the tube's input. On the phone, keep the status line to one line ('4 plans · 3 late' and drop 'Vera is listening' below 30rem). Status's 13px small-caps rule heads are too quiet: set them at the Fraunces head step used on Home, and give the spend tube a live element (a lit tick at today) so P900 has one light. Restaurants, Memory, Family and Wishes still use card cells; move them onto contents lines.

Keep the stem from the tube to NOW, the 'line up.' halo, the bar trace on the tube, the band grid and the 'Also on' index. Fix: shorten the stem's horizontal run by bringing Coming up's rows nearer the tube's x, or drop the stem from the tube's left edge so it does not draw a long bright line across empty ground. Taper its glow after NOW so only NOW to the first row is fully lit. The head-column figures (4 plans, 4 open, 12 ideas) should sit on the first row's baseline. Bring the settings sections onto the page-ground grammar.

Keep the stencil 'plan.' at full tube light, the round radar cut overlapping Next up, the slot glass with day ticks, the engraved seams, the placards and the status foot. Fix: lose the leak bar under 'plan' (it reads as a dash), or widen it into a soft pool with no hard edge. Fill Next up's empty lower half with the location line or the next two plans, so the radar cut is not cutting into nothing. Lower the green share by dimming the slot glass's background bloom, not its ticks. Give the month view one more lit cut beyond today.

Keep the arc route with the lit Now-to-Next leg, the ringed numerals, the readout strip, the pool under 'plan.' and the shape key in the footer. Fix: move the Google note under the rows and let the route and rows run full width, so the empty right column goes. Make the tube larger, or put the Ready chin plate's dot on the tube itself so it is the page's monitor. Bring back the Ideas status filter as a select. The title is the same as Plate's, so give this line its own (keep 'Tell Vera our plan.').

Keep the plates standing on the rail with legs to their ring stops, the lit run from now to stop one, the steel branch of starters and the Status needle inside the glass. Fix: give the greeting box back some light (the lit-from-below edge of Ticked) so the question is read on the tube. Raise the tube so its top meets the box's bottom, closing the gap above Coming up. Show 'Day' on To do consistently on Home and the page.

Keep the Now lamp, the breathing Next ring, the 'pencil' halo and the warm-up trace in the tube. Fix: fill the right column below Something to eat (move Lately added there, or let the shelf end level with Coming up). Space the line's rings further apart. Rename 'Later Lately added' to 'Lately added' alone, with the Later word on the ring.

b.titles: The best are 'What's *on* for us?' (folio-cross) and 'What needs a *plan*?' (sill-cross). Folio-cross's question asks what the service keeps (what is on for the family) in the household's voice, and the lit 'on' is also a power word for a tube, so it is the most phosphor title in the heat. Sill-cross's question cannot be answered 'no' and its lit word sits right above the lit run that answers it. Sill Line, Ticked's 'What needs *planning*?' is close behind. 'Give Vera something to *plan*.' (plate-cross, waypoint-cross) states the job clearly but reads as an order and is now duplicated across two lines. 'Tell Vera what to *line up*.' fits the listing's idea, but 'line up' sounds like scheduling only and loses ideas and wishes. 'What can we *pencil* in?' is charming diary wording but tentative, and in this heat it says the least about Vera's job. 'Tell Vera our *plan*.' presumes a plan already exists.

b.notes:
The crosses beat their parents in every line through this lens, most of all Sill, Folio and Waypoint. They now carry an identity onto Status, Plans and To do, not just Home, which answers the owner's 'reflect more of the page content'.

Features taken across that worked:
- Sill took the main camp's spend needle and lamp board and made them one faceplate. It reads native.
- Folio took the tour's NOW rails and set them as contents lines. Native.
- Waypoint took the main camp's head-row figures. Native, and confident.
- Pocket took the Desk Terminal ledger beside its meter. Native.
- Plate took Waypoint's day numeral and Departures' brass legends. They fit the engraved metal well.

Features that read pasted:
- Listing's round dials are nice objects, but they sit alone in an otherwise flat page.
- Waypoint's footer shape key is fussy.
- Plate's leak dash, and its placards when they repeat on every window.

The two camps compare like this. The tour lines bring drawn structures that do work (rails, routes, the diary line). The main lines bring typographic discipline (rule heads, figure heads). The best crosses marry the two. Folio is the most distinctive art direction and Sill the most complete system.

The phosphor's return: Folio and Sill restrict it best, to the tubes, the one lit word and NOW. Plate keeps the strongest original bloom, at a green share of about 69%.

scores.why: The original tube light is real but it falls evenly over everything. Every block is the same glowing card, so the page reads as 'the Matrix' with no hierarchy or mood beyond the glow.
Desk Terminal is a coherent, calm system with a lovely lit terminal case. Through this lens it is now the safe, familiar baseline: rule heads and lists that any good dark dashboard would have.
Trued has a clear, memorable idea: the week as a lit track with plates standing on it. The inner pages fall back to ordinary ruled tables, so the identity thins out past Home.
The backlit plate has a strong instrument mood, with glass windows cut into slate. Home is still close to the main camp's grammar, and the inner pages are mostly plain lists.

The engraved plate is fully realised: bevelled windows, brass placards that name each scale, the radar cut over Next up's corner, and the spend window and trace joined on Status. It feels like a machined instrument with real character. The month view is plain, and the leak cut under 'plan.' reads as an underline dash.
The listings-page band with its head column is a sound editorial structure. It is quiet to the point of timid: the bands read as a tidy admin table rather than an evening TV guide.

The white-cored stem dropping from the tube to NOW is the most memorable single gesture in the heat, and the round dials on Plans and Status add character. The rest of the page is filled slate bars and generic table rows, so the gesture sits on a fairly stock body.
Folio Switchboard has a genuinely distinctive identity: page numbers, Fraunces numerals and a teletext magazine feel. The tiled grid is busy and boxy, and the huge '900' feels pasted.

This is the most individual voice in the heat. It reads as a graphite almanac: a Fraunces serif title with the halo'd 'on', P-numbers, contents lines with leaders, Fraunces date numerals on a big month sheet, and terminal tubes as the only light. It is editorial rather than dashboard, and it is lovely. The synthesized small caps and the mix of serif, sans, mono and VT323 need a firmer hierarchy.
Its bold Home, with the headline question and a lit wire onto the rail, is memorable. The inner pages are thinner and some details read as gadgets.

Now a whole signal-box system. The board stands on its sill with plates on legs, the starters branch from a junction ring, Status is a graphite faceplate with a lamp board and a moving-coil meter, Ideas has 'the line from home', and Chat is one track ending at 'your turn'. Every page has a drawn idea that does work, and the light sits where the line is live.
It has a warm, personal diary mood and a single line of time. Home is long and list-heavy, and the tube sits like a widget inside it.

It is charming and humane. 'Pencil' is the diary's own word, the ringed lamps run down every page, the slate day tabs are set as a diary sets them, and Plans shows the week list beside a little glass month. It is the most homely identity here, though Home still runs as one long column and the right shelf floats.
The flight-plan route with waypoint rings is an inventive drawing, and the numerals tie the page together. Some of the panel chrome reads as costume.

The route arcs from Now through ringed day numerals are beautiful, and carrying them across the month's cells is the boldest Plans page in the heat. The readout strip and the big title-plus-figure heads give it a confident cockpit tone. Ideas has lost its character to a two-column bullet list, and the title repeats Plate's.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the board on its sill, the steel branch of starters with the junction ring, the Status faceplate (lamp board plus meter), the line from home on Ideas, and Chat as one track ending at 'your turn'. Fix: To do and Lately added are still boxed slate cards under the sill; drop the boxes and hang them as rule-headed lists so the rail stays the only drawn object. The legend line at the foot is a strong idea but reads as an empty rail; give it one lit NOW stop so it echoes the sill. On Plans, the NOW run across the month cells is promising: carry it through to the next plan's row instead of stopping in week one. On the phone, bring Coming up's rail above the fold by setting the branch as a compact single row of keys.

Keep: the Fraunces title with only 'on' lit, the P-numbers, the contents lines with dotted leaders, the Fraunces day numerals on the month sheet, and the tubes as the only light (the Plans countdown tube is excellent). Fix: settle the type hierarchy to three faces with clear jobs (Fraunces for titles and figures, Plex for reading, VT323 only on glass) and replace the synthesized small caps with real Plex Mono caps at 11-12px, tracked. Home's right column ends in a dense 3-up grid of household contents; give it more darkspace, or one contents line per row. Status needs one large Fraunces figure head per group so its first screen has the same contrast as Home.

Keep: 'pencil' in the title, the ringed lamp line on every page, the slate day tabs, the Plans week list beside the glass month, and the Status ledger beside the meter. Fix: Home is one long left column with a short floating shelf; balance it by moving Coming up beside the Next tube, or by widening the shelf to run the full height. Lighten the 'Later / Lately added' doubling by renaming it 'Kept lately'.

Keep: the route arcs with the day numerals in their rings, the route drawn across the month cells, the readout strip, and the title-plus-figure heads. Fix: restore character to Ideas. The two-column bullet list is the weakest page; put the radar's rings or a route from home on it, as Sill did. Choose a title of its own ('Tell Vera our plan.' was this line's voice and distinguishes it from Plate). Fill the empty ground beside Coming up with the month's waypoint mini-route rather than one Google note.

Keep: the engraved plate, the brass placards naming each scale, the radar window cut over Next up, the joined spend-and-trace slot on Status, and the pinhole lamp banks. Fix: lose the leak dash under 'plan.' (it reads as an underline) and let the stencil's own halo carry it. Give the month view a lit window per plan day, not only today. The starter keys under the box feel like generic tabs; engrave them as a row of plate keys flush with the box's foot.

Keep: the stem from the tube to NOW, the head column with its figure, and the round dials on Plans and Status. Fix: the body under the stem is filled slate bars; switch rows to page ground with leaders, as a printed listing would set them, and put the evening's times in a column of their own so the TV-listing idea shows. Set the To do figure on the first row's baseline. The Ideas filter sidebar of grey keys is stock; set it as a listing's index.

b.titles: The best is 'What's on for us?' (Folio). It is the family's own idiom, it names what the service keeps (what's on), and it suits the almanac voice. The serif with one lit word is the most characterful greeting in the heat. A close second is 'What can we pencil in?' (Pocket): it is warm, specific to a diary, and 'pencil' is a lovely lit verb. 'What needs a plan?' (Sill) is clear and inviting and cannot be answered 'no', though it is plainer than the parent's 'What needs planning?'. 'Give Vera something to plan.' works but is now used by both Plate and Waypoint, which costs each its identity; Waypoint should go back to 'Tell Vera our plan.' The weakest is 'Tell Vera what to line up.' (Listing): 'line up' is a pun on the listing that the family would not say, and it sounds like an order rather than an invitation.

b.notes: Every cross beat its carried design through this lens, and the two main-camp lines that struggled most gained most. Folio (+1.5) went from costume to the clearest system in the heat by taking the tour's rails with one lit NOW and the main camp's head-row principle. Listing gained by taking Sill's lit wire, rebuilt as a stem from the tube to NOW. It is the best example of a graft made its own: it joins the hero to the list, and it makes the light mean 'from now'. Grafts that worked: the needle meter with ghost, now on Status in sill, pocket and waypoint (one meter vocabulary; the panel could standardise it); rule heads replacing bays (waypoint, sill); the shape law and footer key from Dessau (waypoint's is the cleaner, since sill's legend rail costs space); square ticks (sill, waypoint); the placarded slot scope reused across pages (plate). Grafts that read pasted: pocket's boxed right-hand cards (main-camp panels on a design whose idea is no boxes); listing's Plans dial (a third dial style); plate's stencil leak; sill's foot rail. The camps converge: the tour brings lines and rails that tie lists to time, and the main camp brings page heads with figures, rule heads and calm Status sheets. The best crosses (folio, waypoint, listing) combine a time rail with a figure head row. That pairing is a candidate standard: every page opens on title + figure + one primary; every list in time hangs from a rail with one lit NOW; light only in tubes, lamps and the key word. Watch the phones: waypoint's readout above the box and sill's plates below the fold both delay the main job. Afterglow is still invisible in the details strips for every design.

scores.why: One undifferentiated green-on-black card grid: no type steps, every box the same weight, green as both brand and every state. The light is authentic but spent everywhere, so nothing leads.

A clear system: the numbered section heads, the terminal tube as the one lit object, a Ready foot on every page. It is still boxes inside boxes, the side column repeats on every page, and the greeting lost its pool of light.

One coherent device, the lit line with ring stops, holds Home, To do, the month and the chat, with a proper page-head rule. Plates sit on slate panels, so it is box-heavy, and the status console is good but dense.
The scarce-light law is right and the rule heads are clean, but the page reads as one plain long sheet. Status is a bare column and the slot tubes repeat without labels.

Now a real system: seams between bands, page heads carrying their figures (Status 5 working · 1 needs a look · 7 off), a placarded slot scope on Plans, To do and Coming up, and a rebuilt Status with spend tube and 30-day trace. Green share is still high, the stencil leak reads as a dash, and the full-width Send on the phone is heavy.
The head-column band grid and leader rows are a sound, extensible listing grammar. It is flat and dim: the bands are near-identical slabs, and the setup row's bronze fill reads as selected.

The lit stem from Next up's tube down to NOW is the best cross-camp graft in the heat: it joins the hero to the list and gives light a job. The band grid now holds the chat, Ideas filters, Status (a round spend dial) and To do. Rows as filled slate strips are heavy, and the Plans dial floating in the head column is a one-off.
Rich figure-setting and a real page-number system, but 96px folios, card-cell grids, caps nav and buttons, and cards everywhere make it costume more than a system.

The biggest transformation and the most legible system: every page opens on one head row (P-number, Fraunces title, figure, one green primary), every list is a contents line, and every timed list hangs from a rail with one lit NOW. Fraunces with Plex is the best type pairing in the heat, the radar draws the rows by their day, and the light sits only in the tube and the lamps. Weak spots: numbered nav suffixes add noise, the placeholder glows inside the tube, and Home's lower directory block is small and busy.

The headline question and the wire dropping onto the rail are strong, and the To do ticks as stops are clever. But ring ticks read as lamps, not controls, and the setup strip and Status console are crowded.

Reads top to bottom with one type system: square ticks, the steel branch of starters, plates standing on the rail, a fine needle meter on Status, and the lamp key in every foot. The foot's legend rail takes a lot of dark ground, Home's lower panels are boxed again, and the plates hide below the fold on the phone.
The one steel line of time and diary-set dates make a strong, quiet, distinctive system. Square nodes are confused with tick boxes, and the Now tags are dashed.

Rings now do the work, the Status needle meter is good, and the dates stay beautiful. But Home's right column became three boxed cards, which breaks the 'hangs from the line without boxes' idea, the phone's 'More' menu hides the bar's icons, and the change from Kept is small.
The waypoint rings carrying the day numerals are a superb joining device, and the readout strip is good. Bays, lamp-like ticks and outlined stat boxes make it busier than its idea needs.

A written shape law (ring = light, square = yours, bar = page's, triangle = look) keyed in the footer; rule heads replace bays; big figure page heads (Ideas 12, Status 5, Plans 4); the month carries the rings; Status is one calm sheet with a needle meter. The phone puts the readout strip above the box, Ideas' two-column list loses its scan line, and To do's row edges are amber-heavy.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP: the single head row (P-number, Fraunces title, light Fraunces figure with small-caps unit, one green primary); contents lines; the NOW rail with amber late dots; the radar plotting each plan by its day; the Fraunces-on-Plex pairing; the /tasks tally tube. FIX: (1) Bar: drop the page-number suffixes from the nav (keep P-numbers in the page heads only); they double the nav's noise and repeat the caps-and-numbers failure. (2) Home greeting: the placeholder sits in a lit green frame inside the tube; per 'the family's words stay matte', make the field slate until typed in, and keep the halo on 'on' and the status line. (3) Home's lower directory (Wishes/Memory/Family/Status/Settings) is a busy 3+2 grid of small cells; make it one contents list (number · name · leader · state) like Settings. (4) Pick one cross-reference device: small caps or italic 'see p400', not both. (5) Carry the head row and contents lines to Restaurants, Memory, Family and Wishes, which still use card cells. (6) Status: lift the rule heads to 15px Fraunces like Home's section heads, so the page's first screen has hierarchy.

KEEP: the shape law and its footer key; the waypoint rings carrying the day numeral in the route, at the row's head and in the month cell; rule heads; the big figure page heads; Status as one sheet with the needle; square ticks. FIX: (1) Phone: move the Today/Plans/To do/Late/Ideas readout below the box; the question must lead to the field. (2) Ideas: go back to one-column rows with a right-aligned drive column; the two-column wrapped cards lose the scan line, and the square kind bullets clash with the 'square = yours' rule (a square that is not pressable). Use the kind colour on a bar. (3) To do: the amber 3px edge plus a triangle plus amber words is three signals for one state; keep the triangle and words and drop the edge. (4) Home: fill or close the empty 150px beside Coming up (move the Google note under the rows and widen them). (5) Restore a 'planned/done' filter as keys beside 'Show dropped'.

KEEP: the lit stem from the tube to NOW (the heat's best graft); the head column with figure and links; leader rows to tabular facts; the round spend dial on Status; the same band grid on chat, Ideas and To do. FIX: (1) Rows: drop the filled slate behind every row, and use hairline leaders on page ground with a hover wash, so bands breathe. (2) Set the head-column figure on the first row's baseline. (3) The Plans 'Next in 2 days' dial is a third dial style; reuse the Status dial or drop it for the slot. (4) The setup strip's amber left bar plus ringed steps is good; keep amber for late only (use bone for the bar). (5) Convert the settings section pages to the page-ground grammar. (6) Title: see titles.

KEEP: question, box, then the sill; plates standing on the rail lit only to stop one; the starter branch; square ticks; the Status needle with ghost; one type system. FIX: (1) The foot's lamp key on a long empty rail costs about 80px of dark ground per page; set it as one short line beside the footer mark. (2) Home's To do and Lately added sit in boxed panels again; put them on ground under rule heads, as the main camp's rule heads intended. (3) Phone: bring the rail and the first plate above the fold by tightening the box (one-line placeholder). (4) Status's lamp console text is tiny (labels about 10px); raise it to the 12px floor.

KEEP: seams, page heads with figures and states, the placarded slot scope reused on Plans, To do and Coming up, the Status spend tube and 30-day trace, the starter tabs labelled PLANS/TO DO/IDEAS, diary day numerals with month/day. FIX: (1) Remove the stencil leak under 'plan.', which reads as an underline or dash; let the halo carry it. (2) Phone: Send is full width and as loud as the title; return it to the row with From. (3) Dim the slot glass's outer bloom to cut the green share, and keep the full strength for the radar and Send only. (4) Month view: give the plans in cells the slot's tick colour and number, so the scope and grid join. (5) Settings: avoid the odd full-width Sign-in group.

KEEP: the 2px line with ring lamps, diary-set dates on tabs, the needle meter, 'Now' as a lit lamp. FIX: (1) Take Home's right column out of boxes and hang it from its own line with rings, as Kept did. (2) Phone: restore the bar's icons instead of 'More'. (3) The 'pencil' title glows on 7 letters at display size; shorten it (see titles). (4) Status's meter case is heavy; thin it to a 2px bezel.

b.titles: The best is "Give Vera something to plan." (plate and waypoint). It names who listens and the job, and it covers weekends, reminders and ideas. Its lit word is short, and the full stop sits in the lit run. "What's on for us?" (folio) is a close second: a warm question that fits the whole service (plans, to-dos, ideas), and a two-letter lit word gives a tidy halo. It could, though, be heard as 'show me what's on', a reading request, against the box's job. "What needs a plan?" (sill) is good: it cannot be answered no and is shorter than 'planning'. "Tell Vera what to line up." (listing) fails: 'line up' is a softer idiom than plan, the two-word lit run is heavy, and 'what to line up' reads like queueing, not planning. "What can we pencil in?" (pocket) is charming and on theme, but it suggests only tentative diary entries (not reminders or ideas), and 'pencil' is a heavy lit word. The carried titles: "What's on your mind?" is generic and is the original's; "Tell Vera our plan." presumes a plan exists; "What's our plan?" is fine but reads as asking to be shown; "What needs planning?" carries too much glow.

b.notes: Through this lens every cross beat its carried design, mostly because they share one structural gain: rule heads with a figure and a link at the right, 44px targets everywhere (folio's cross fixed the parent's 4 to 20 small targets per page), and a NOW line on To do. Borrowings that worked: waypoint's readout strip combined with main-camp rule heads and the Ready foot, which gives the fastest glance in the heat; plate's lamp strip with a legend (from Trued) and its destination legends on starters (from Departures), both of which reduce guessing; listing's lit stem from Sill Line, which ties the tube to its list better than any legend, and its 'Also on' index from Settled Light; sill's lamp key in the foot and its rule heads. Borrowings that read pasted: plate's scale placards, which are instrument jargon a family will not read; folio's page numbers inside every link; sill's plates stacked beside a Next tube, a second drawing of the same list; pocket's slate day tabs, which add weight without information. Comparing the camps: the tour lines bring better time drawings (rails, rings, numerals tied to rows) and the main lines bring better page structure (head rows, rule heads, status foot), and the best crosses are where those meet (waypoint, sill, plate). Light now sits mostly where attention belongs (the title word, Send, Next up, NOW), and none of the crosses glare. Recurring problems: titles underlined at rest (waypoint), the phone fold hiding the week (sill, pocket), and empty right-column ground beside Coming up (waypoint, pocket).

scores.why: The card grid reads as a pile when blurred, 42 of 55 Home targets are under 44px, and To do is boxed cards with ISO dates and folded actions. The title, box and Send are clear, but nothing below them has a sight line.

Leader yardstick. The terminal and box are one clear first stop, rule heads carry their figures and links, and every target is 44px. Status's numbered contents column is quick to scan, but Home's right column is a dense stack of four equal heads.

Tour yardstick. Its strength is the lit rail that reads Now to the next stop at a glance, and the branch of starters says plainly what each one does. Coming up's plates hang under the rail, though, and the eye has to zig-zag from rail to card to date.

Calm and legible, with a clear title, box and Send, and rule heads with figures. Home is one long undifferentiated sheet, Status is one bare column, and the slot window draws marks that are not tied to the rows.

The seams finally split Home into readable bands, and the starters are full keys with a brass destination underneath (PLANS / TO DO / IDEAS), which tells a newcomer where each one leads. Status opens with a head tally, then a joined spend and 30-day screen, then a lamp strip with a legend, so it is answered in one glance. The status foot answers 'is it working?' on every page. It loses points for the placard jargon ('PLANS · RINGS 1·2·4 WK', '1 WK/DIV') and for the leak cut under 'plan', which reads as a stray dash.

The head column with a big figure gives each band a clear label, and every row is a leader line to its facts, so it is easy to scan. The first screen is busy, though: the tube's chart, the setup box and the starters compete, and Coming up sits below the fold.

There is now one left edge on every page. The stem from the tube to NOW visibly says 'this tube is the first row below', which no other design manages so plainly. 'Also on' ends Home as an index to every other page with its live facts, the best wayfinding in the heat. The 13rem head column costs measure and leaves the figures floating, and 'line up' is a muddier verb than 'plan'.

The numbered service is a novel way to find a page, but it has small targets (4 on Home, 20 on To do) and the dense grid of P-numbers. On top of that, the box is buried inside the tube under the radar, so the first action is hard to find.

Every target is now at least 44px, Status's contents lines (lamp, number, name, leader, state) read well, and To do hangs from a clear NOW rail. Page numbers on every nav key and in 'see p400 Plans' add codes the family has to decode. The title asks to be shown what is on rather than to be told, so the box's job is muddled.

The headline question, box and lit rail are a strong first read, and To do's stops are the ticks you press, which is a direct mapping. The lit 'planning' halo is heavy, Coming up's cards sit tight under the rail, and the setup strip is busy.

Home reads cleanly as question, then box beside a labelled 'OR START WITH' branch, then the week standing on one rail with day numerals under the stops. The lamp legend in every foot explains the marks, and To do's Day / Thing / Who / Due columns with square ticks are the clearest list in the heat. On the other hand, the Next tube and the three slate plates are two different drawings for one list. On a phone the rail falls below the fold.
The one line of time from Now to Later is easy to follow, and diary-set dates are quick to read. The shelf is an unrelated second column, and on a phone Next and Coming up are pushed well down.

The stops (Now, Finish setting up, Next, Coming up, Later) make Home's order explicit, and the sticky To do on the right is a good place to look. Ringed lamps with amber late rings code state clearly. Coming up's tabs are dense, 'Later' beside 'Lately added' trips the eye, and on a phone the Next tube is barely on the first screen.

The readout strip gives the counts at a glance, and the day numeral ties each row to its route ring. The bays box everything, Settings keeps icon gutters, and the first screen is crowded with a placard under every instrument.

The best at-a-glance page. The title, box and Send come first; then the readout strip (Today, Plans 4, To do 4, Late 3, Ideas 12) answers 'how are we doing' before any scrolling. The route's numbered rings match the big numerals leading each row, and the foot keys the four shapes. The phone keeps the strip right under the title. Faults: every Coming up title is underlined at rest, which is noisy, the Ideas kind keys wrap into two rows, and the empty ground beside Coming up.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the readout strip as the welcome's foot; the ringed numerals tied to the row numerals; the rule heads with figure and link at the right; the Ready foot; the shape legend. Fix Home: take the underline off row titles at rest, so the underline shows only on hover and focus with the steel afterglow. Fill the empty right column beside Coming up with the Next leg's 'in 2 days' readout or the Google note set as a band foot, or let the rows run to 46rem and drop the column. Fix Ideas: make the kind keys one scrollable row or a select, so the table starts higher. Fix To do: give back a Show filter for planned and done (a select beside the 'Show dropped' key). Fix Settings: say 'needs a look' once, in the caution line only. Give the form page its own rule head.

Keep: the seams between bands; starters as keys with destination legends; the head tally plus lamp strip and legend on Status; the status foot on every page; whole-row targets. Fix: rewrite the placards in plain words ('Next 4 weeks', 'Spend, last 30 days') instead of 'RINGS 1·2·4 WK' and '1 WK/DIV'. Make the leak under 'plan' an obvious pool of light rather than a short bar, or drop it. Give Next up's screen a fixed lower-left text area so a long location never runs under the round window. Number the slot's marks, which it already does in VT323, and ring the matching row numeral when that row is hovered. On the setup band, underline only the verb phrase, not the whole sentence.

Keep: question, then box beside the 'Or start with' branch; the sill rail with day numerals under the stops; To do's Day/Thing/Who/Due columns and square ticks; the legend in the foot. Fix Home: draw Next up and the later plans in one grammar, either all as plates on the rail with Next as the lit plate, or the tube alone with rows under it, so one list is not drawn twice. On a phone, move the rail above the branch, or fold the starters into a row of three keys, so the week shows on the first screen. On To do, keep the 'Day' head as Home does. Move the ghost needle's 'avg' label clear of the hot needle at low values.

Keep: the stem from tube to NOW; the single left edge; the head column with figure and links; 'Also on' as an index of every page with live facts; starters saying where they usually go. Fix: narrow the head column to about 10rem and set the figure on the first row's baseline, so the rows get measure and the figure reads as that list's count. Put the setup strip above Coming up, or keep it but give it the same band grid. Bring the settings section pages onto the page-ground band grammar. On the new-idea form, put the Title before the kind keys in Tab order. Reconsider the title verb (see titles).

Keep: the stops naming Home's order (Now, Setup, Next, Coming up, Later); amber late rings; the sticky To do column; the Status ledger beside the meter. Fix: rename the 'Later' stop beside 'Lately added', for example by setting the head alone as 'Lately added' on the Later ring. On a phone, put Next directly under the box and shorten the box (one-line placeholder), so the tube's top is clearly on the first screen. Lighten Coming up's slate day tabs so the dates, not the tabs, carry the rows.

Keep: the contents-line grammar on Status (lamp, number, name, leader, state); the NOW rail on To do; the head row with figure and primary; 44px targets throughout. Fix: drop page numbers from the nav keys and from 'see p400 Plans', or keep them only as a faint index on page heads, because they are codes the family has to learn. Change the title to an invitation to tell Vera, since 'What's on for us?' asks to be shown. Take the box out of the tube so the field is a plain, obvious control with the tube's status line above it.

b.titles: The best are 'Give Vera something to plan.' (plate-cross, waypoint-cross) and 'What needs a plan?' (sill-cross). Both say plainly that the box is where you hand things over and that planning is the job. 'Give Vera...' names who hears you and invites any kind of item, and 'What needs a plan?' cannot be answered 'no' and carries a short lit word that sits right above the plans that answer it. 'What can we pencil in?' (pocket-cross) is warm and on concept, but 'pencil in' sounds tentative and calendar-only, so it undersells reminders and ideas. 'Tell Vera what to line up.' (listing-cross) has the right shape, but 'line up' is vague (queue? schedule?) and the lit run is two words. 'What's on for us?' (folio-cross) fails here: it reads as asking the page to show the schedule, the opposite of the box's job. Among the carried titles, 'What's on your mind?' is generic, 'What's our plan?' presumes a plan exists, 'What needs planning?' is a heavy eight-letter halo, and 'Tell Vera our plan.' is fine but narrower than 'something to plan'.

b.notes: Through a typesetter's eye, every cross beats its carried parent, and most of the gain is in how figures and dates are set. The feature that crossed best is the day numeral as one glyph, taken by Plate from Waypoint and echoed by Folio's oldstyle Fraunces numerals and Pocket's diary tabs: a light large figure with month and weekday stacked beside it, leading To do's due column and the Plans rows. It reads as the house's own way of setting a date, not as a paste, and it should become the standard. Rule heads with the figure and link at the right, taken by Waypoint and Sill from the main camp, also travelled well. Pasted-looking: Plate's tracked-caps brass placards (a fourth label style at 12px), Waypoint's mono dates under the 'Was due' lines, Listing's mono phrases, and Folio's page numbers in the nav. On display faces: condensed heads (Archivo or Plex Condensed) suit the phosphor; Waypoint's wide Plex 600 greeting is the odd one out. Folio's Fraunces is the boldest pairing and works because it is kept to titles and figures, never to rows. Camps: the main camp's crosses (Plate, Folio) brought the richer type systems; the tour's crosses (Sill, Waypoint, Pocket) brought more disciplined date and numeral rules. The best standard would combine Plate's six-step scale, Sill's one-face-per-job rule, Waypoint's one-numeral law and Folio's figure-plus-unit head row. Bringing back the original light is handled typographically in Folio (the halo on one word) and Plate (the stencil), and both keep the body matte, which is right. No cross sets body text below 15px, and none uses the original's tiny grey card text.

scores.why: Flat hierarchy: small titles barely above body, ISO dates and 19:56 seconds-level stamps in To do cards, labels and facts in one grey, no figure system. Legible, but it is not typeset.
Condensed head over Plex with tabular facts and a clean title-figure-unit head row; let down by whole phrases in tracked mono ('was due 5 days ago') and a busy small-text column on Status.
Calm, consistent scale and good counts-beside-title head; the day labels on the rail are small and the Status tally line is a run of same-size figures with no step between them.

The 40px condensed question with a true curly apostrophe and the rule heads carrying a figure and link at the right are good; every setup row underlined at rest and long flat lists make the body read as one grey block.

The best-built type system in the heat: six real steps (12/15/17/22/30/44), condensed heads on engraved rule lines, and one engraved day numeral (30px Plex Mono with month and weekday stacked) that leads Coming up, Plans and To do's due column, so dates line up as figures. Underlines only on hover lift the setup list; the brass tracked-caps placards are small and the leak dash under 'plan' reads as a typographic underline.

Head column with a figure over its label is a real listing device, and leaders run to tabular times; but each row says the date twice ('9 OCT FRI' and 'Friday 9 October'), and the head-column prose wraps to a ragged 6-word measure.

Removing the duplicate date fixed the rows: day numeral, stacked mono month/weekday, Plex title, leader, tabular time and 'in 2 days' is clean listing setting. To do still sets 'was due 5 days ago' as a whole tracked-mono phrase, the head-column figure floats under its head instead of on the first row's baseline, and the head column leaves the title and its icon tile far apart.

Fraunces figures (oldstyle day numerals, raised units) are the most beautiful setting in the field, but the 96px thin folios are costume, the VT323 question on glass is hard to read at body size, and the buttons are tracked caps.

The strongest typographic voice here: Fraunces page titles with a light Fraunces figure and small-caps unit ('4 OPEN · 3 LATE'), oldstyle Fraunces day numerals in the Plans rail and To do's due column, contents lines with dotted leaders, and the 96px folios gone. Against it: the nav's grey page-number suffixes ('Home 100') crowd every key, synthesized small caps at 13px look thin, and the italic cross-references ('see p400 Plans') add a second label device.
Good to put the question first as a headline, but eight lit letters of 'planning' at display size make a glare block, and the plates' titles break awkwardly ('Mount St. / Helens day trip').

One type system written once: Archivo 75% width for display, title and head, DM Sans body at 1/1.55, DM Mono kept to clock times, day numerals and margin dates; counts sit on their title's baseline ('Things to do 4 open · 3 late'). The compact lit 'plan' fixes the glare; small tracked-caps column heads (DONE, THING TO DO) and VT323 lamp names on Status are the weak spots.
Diary-set dates on the line are a fine idea, but titles of setup steps wrap at a cramped measure in the right column and the large 'Now'/'Next' plates are heavier than the type they mark.

Diary tabs ('27 Sep / Sun' with a light numeral) and the Status ledger with tabular Plex Mono figures in one column are careful, real typesetting; the big condensed bone title is handsome. The '4 open · 3 late' count floats far right away from its title, the 'Later Lately added' pairing stutters, and on the phone the title breaks to two lines with 'pencil in?' split.

One Plex family, clear readout strip with dotted leaders to figures, day numerals in the waypoint rings; the 40px light numerals are good but title weights are generic and the setup line runs one long grey measure.

Shows the one-numeral rule best: Plex 500 in the ring, 300 at 40px leading the row, 22px in the month cell, all tabular, and the head row 'Things to do 4 open / ▲3 late' with the stacked unit on the title's baseline is excellent. The 48px greeting in non-condensed Plex 600 is wide and plain beside the condensed heads elsewhere, 'Was due' capitalised breaks the lowercase used everywhere else, and the mono date under it ('Sun 27 Sep') makes a third style in one cell.

fixes.suggestion: Keep the six-step scale, the engraved day numeral leading every dated list, the rule heads with figure+link at the right, and underline-on-hover-only rows. Fix: on Home turn the stencil's leak cut into a soft pool with no hard edge, so it stops reading as an underline under 'plan'. Lift the brass placards and destination legends from 12px tracked caps to 12-13px small caps at +4% tracking, or sentence case, because at this size they shimmer. In To do, move '#4' after the title in --faint, as Folio does, so titles align on their first letter, and set 'was due 5 days ago' on the same baseline as the title column's second line, not indented. Give Status' head tally a step between the figure (30px) and its unit (13px label ink) so '5 working · 1 needs a look · 7 off' does not read as one run.

Keep Fraunces for titles and figures only (light figure + small-caps unit), oldstyle day numerals in the rails, and contents lines with leaders. Fix: drop the page-number suffixes from the nav keys (keep the P-number only in each page's head row), because they double the nav's text and cramp it. Replace synthesized small caps with real ones: Fraunces' own smcp, or Plex at 600 13px with +6% tracking, not scaled caps. Choose one cross-reference device (italic sentence case) and use it everywhere the small-caps label currently stands in for a reference. Raise Status' rule heads to the Fraunces 22px cell-head step used on Home, so the first screen has a hierarchy. Keep 'on' lit, but see titles.

Keep the single system (Archivo 75% heads, DM Sans body 1/1.55, DM Mono only for clock times and day numerals) and counts on the title's baseline. Fix: set To do's column heads in sentence case 12px label ink rather than tracked caps, and put 'Day' back or drop it on Home too, so both say the same. Replace the VT323 row names on Status's lamp board with DM Mono, because VT323 at that size is the one place legibility drops. Rewrap the plate titles with text-wrap: balance so 'Mount St. Helens / day trip' does not break after 'St.'.

Keep the one-numeral law (ring, row lead, month cell) and the head row with its stacked unit on the title's baseline. Fix: set the greeting in the same Condensed 600 as the rule heads, at 44-48px, so the page has one display face; this also keeps 'Give Vera something to plan.' to two clean lines on a phone. Lowercase 'was due' to match the rest, and set the date under it in Plex Sans tabular at label size instead of mono, so a cell carries two styles, not three. Make the Ideas Kind keys nowrap with smaller padding so the rack is one line.

Keep the diary tabs, the light day numeral on slate, and the Status ledger in tabular Plex Mono. Fix: bring '4 open · 3 late' to the title's baseline beside 'Things to do' instead of the far right edge. Rename 'Later Lately added' to 'Later · Added lately', or drop the ring's word, so the two words do not stutter. On the phone set the title with text-wrap: balance so 'pencil in?' stays together.

Keep the listing row: numeral, stacked month/weekday, Plex title, leader, tabular time and relative time. Fix: in To do set 'was due 5 days ago' in Plex Sans amber, not tracked mono (mono for the time figure only). Put the head-column figure on the first row's baseline. Pull the page title into the head column beside its tile, or move the tile to the title's x, so the head reads as one unit. Light only 'up' or rework the title, since a two-word lit run and its lit full stop make a long glow block.

b.titles: The best titles are 'Give Vera something to plan.' (Plate, Engraved; Waypoint, Ruled) and 'What needs a plan?' (Sill, Squared). Each says the job, which is to hand Vera anything and get a plan back. Each ends on a short four-letter lit word, so the halo stays compact, and both fix their lines' old problems ('planning' was too heavy, 'our plan' presumed a plan already existed). 'Give Vera something to plan.' names who hears you and works as an invitation, but at 48px it runs long and wraps to two lines on a phone. 'What needs a plan?' is the tighter line, cannot be answered 'no', and sits well over the lit run of plans. 'What can we pencil in?' (Pocket, Lit) is charming and fits the diary, but the lit word sits mid-line rather than at the end, 'pencil in' makes everything sound tentative, and on a phone the line breaks between 'pencil' and 'in'. 'Tell Vera what to line up.' (Listing) is a weaker version of the proven 'Tell Vera what to plan.': 'line up' also means a queue, and the two lit words plus the lit full stop make a long glow block. 'What's on for us?' (Folio) fails. It asks the app to show the schedule, the opposite of the box's job, and its lit word 'on' is a preposition that carries no meaning, however lovely the Fraunces setting is. Among the carried titles, 'What needs planning?' is too heavy, 'What's our plan?' presumes a plan exists, and 'What's on your mind?' is generic.

b.notes:
The crosses beat their carried lines on every count through this lens; every one gained 0.4-1.5. The biggest jump is Folio, whose crossing replaced cards with contents lines and a single head row. Imports that worked:
- The main camp's rule heads and one head row per page (Waypoint, Folio, Sill) gave every inner page the same 'title · count · primary' shape, the clearest consistency gain of the round.
- The day numeral leading rows (Plate from Waypoint) makes 'when' readable at a glance on To do and Coming up.
- The status foot / Ready line (Plate, Waypoint from Joined) answers 'is it working' everywhere without opening Status.
- Starters labelled with their destination (Plate's 'PLANS', Listing's 'usually Plans' from Departures) tell a first-timer what each does.
- The single setup strip with its next step named (Sill, Listing, Waypoint, Pocket) replaces long boxed lists.
- The readout strip and NOW lines carry state.
Imports that read pasted: Listing's lit stem, a long decorative wire the eye follows to nowhere; Plate's placards in oscilloscope units; Folio's page numbers in the bar, which are flavour, not wayfinding; Pocket's second Next tube on Home's line, which duplicates Next up. Camps: the tour finals arrive with stronger state-marking ideas (lamp legends, rings that mean one thing, ticks you press), while the main camp brings the calmer page structure (rule heads, head rows, unboxed lists). The crosses that took the main camp's structure onto a tour idea (Waypoint, Sill) or the tour's state marks onto a main structure (Folio's rails and lamps) are the most usable. No cross removed a needed task except Waypoint's Ideas Status filter (planned/done now only by URL), a small but real cost. Legibility: all crosses keep 13px minimum text (Sill is 12px on the phone), with 0 targets under 44px on Home. Waypoint's minimum contrast is 4.64, the lowest in the heat, still above AA.

scores.why: Every task can be done, but Home is a stack of equally loud boxed cards, To do is cards with a 'Edit, complete, or snooze' disclosure on each, and Status is three boxes of prose, so a tired eye has to read everything to find what is late.

Desk Terminal, Joined: clear one-column lists with WHO/DUE heads and a NOW line on To do. But Home puts the ask box inside the tube under Next up, so the box is not the first thing you see, and 'Ready' sits in the side column on every page.

Trued, Relit: the ways to start as a labelled branch and the lamp board's single tally make the state readable at a glance. The month rail and the plate cards on Home's line are small, and To do's date column is cramped.
Backlit Plate: the lists are clean, but the Plans and To do slots are thin strips of glass that say little to a first-time user, and on Status the spend screen floats far from the lists it explains.

Big gains: setup is three full-sentence links you can click, To do's large day numerals put due dates where the eye lands, the status foot answers 'is it working?' on every page, and the starter keys say where each lands (PLANS / TO DO / IDEAS). Costs: placards like 'PLANS · RINGS 1·2·4 WK' and '1 WK/DIV' are jargon to a parent, the radar cut over the Next up corner crowds a long location, and Ideas hides For and Status behind a 'For anyone · Any but dropped' disclosure.

Evening Listing: the head column with a big count and links ('3 late →', 'All 4') is a very fast way in. But the filters on Ideas and To do are a nest of side keys that take a minute to learn, and the setup band is long.

The most scannable Home in the heat: every band is count, link, then rows with leaders to tabular facts. The starter keys say 'usually Plans / To do / Ideas', setup is one strip with 'Next: choose your own password', and 'Also on' gives a one-click index of the rest of the app. The lit stem from the tube to NOW is a long detour that the eye follows for nothing, and the page is long, about 2000px. Settings' inner pages still use the old panels.
Folio Switchboard: huge page numbers ('500', '990') take the space where the title should be, To do is a grid of cards, so ticking and comparing due dates is slow, and Settings is nine boxed tiles.

A real usability turnaround. Each page opens on one head row with its count and one green primary. Lists are contents lines with right-aligned state. Settings puts 'Sign-in and security · Needs a look' first. Restaurants is one key at the end of the kind row. The status line on the tube ('4 plans · 3 late · Vera is listening') tells you the state before you type. Costs: page numbers in the nav and 'see p400 Plans' hints are noise for a parent who has never read teletext, and the focused select in the details strip has no ring.
Sill Line, Ticked: the question as the board's headline makes the start obvious, but the Coming up plates on the rail are tiny and the setup strip's tick track is hard to read.

Home reads top to bottom: question, box, the ways to start (each a 44px slate key with an arrow), Next up, then the week. Setup is one strip with 'Next: choose your own password'. The To do table has DAY/WHO/DUE heads and square ticks, and the lamp legend in the footer explains every mark once. The plate cards in Coming up repeat the kind as tracked caps and push times into small chips, and on the phone the plans are below the fold.
Pocket Diary, Kept: diary-set dates are easy to read, but the second NEXT UP tube in the line, the run-ons, and the many stops crowd Home. Status's marks need a legend to decode.

To do's quick-add field at the top of the page is the fastest way to add a task in the heat, the right column on Home lists late tasks with their WHO, and 'No date' fills the hole on To do. But Home puts the ask box, setup, a Next stop, a second tube and Coming up on one long line, so the plans start below 800px. 'Later Lately added' reads oddly, and the phone bar folds Memory, Family, Status and Settings into 'More', one more tap.

Waypoint Lamps: the readout strip (Plans 4, To do 4, Late 3, Ideas 12) is excellent. But the Plans month is a route of arcs over the cells that hides where a day's plans are, and Status splits into small panels.

The best glanceable Home: the readout strip answers 'what is overdue' (▲ Late 3) before any list, the setup line names its next step, the route with day rings ties to big day numerals leading rows with 'Next · in 2 days', and late tasks carry an amber edge plus a triangle and words, so colour is never the only signal. The shape key in the footer teaches the marks once. Costs: Ideas lost its Status filter (planned/done only by URL), the Plans month arcs and dotted stubs still clutter the cells, and on the phone the readout strip pushes the box down.

fixes.suggestion: KEEP the readout strip (Today / Plans / To do / ▲ Late / Ideas), and make each figure a link: Late 3 opens To do filtered to late. Keep the day numeral leading every row, the amber edge with triangle and words for late, and the footer shape key. FIX Ideas: restore the Status filter as a row of latched keys (Any but dropped / Planned / Done / Dropped) beside Kind, rather than only 'Show dropped'. FIX Plans month: drop the arcs and dotted stubs inside the cells, and keep only the ringed day numeral and a plain plan chip, with the route on the strip above the grid. PHONE: put the box straight under the title and the readout strip under the box, so typing to Vera is on the first screen. Fill the empty right column under Coming up with Next up's details or the setup line instead of the lone Google note.

KEEP the single head row per page (title, count, one green primary), the contents lines with right-aligned state, 'Needs a look' sorted first in Settings, and the tube's status line. FIX: take the page numbers out of the top bar, or show them only on hover or focus. Change 'see p400 Plans' under the starters to 'lands in Plans', the plain words a parent reads without knowing teletext. Give the focused select the same halo ring as the field and Send. Bring Restaurants (310), Memory, Family and Wishes onto contents lines so one kind of list looks one way everywhere. On the phone, let the status line on the glass truncate to one line, and put 'Send where I am' on the From row so the starters rise onto the first screen.

KEEP the top-to-bottom Home (question, box, ways-to-start branch with 44px keys), the one-strip setup with its next step, To do's DAY/WHO/DUE table with square ticks, and the lamp legend in every footer. FIX Coming up plates: drop the tracked-caps kind line, set the time at the body size and not in a boxed chip, and make the whole plate the link. Show 'Day' on the To do page as Home does (consistency). On the phone, move the Next up tube above the branch, or fold the branch into a horizontal scroll row, so a plan is on the first screen. On Status, set the 'avg' label clear of the hot needle.

KEEP the starter keys with their destination ('PLANS / TO DO / IDEAS'), setup as full-sentence links, To do's large day numerals in the due column, and the status foot on every page. FIX: replace the placards' instrument jargon ('PLANS · RINGS 1·2·4 WK', 'DUE · 1 WK/DIV') with family words ('Rings: 1, 2 and 4 weeks away'), or remove them where the axis already says '1 wk'. On Ideas, show For and Status as visible selects next to Search rather than behind a disclosure. Take the radar off Next up's corner, or move it below, so a long place name never collides. The short leak under 'plan' reads as a stray dash: drop it or make it the full width of the word.

KEEP the head column (count, '3 late →', 'All 4'), the leader rows to tabular facts, 'usually Plans' on the starters, and 'Also on' as an index. FIX: shorten the lit stem so it drops from the tube straight onto NOW instead of running across 500px of empty ground. Tighten the bands' vertical padding so Lately added is reached sooner. Move the settings section pages to the same band grammar. On the new-idea form, put Title before the kind keys in Tab order.

KEEP the quick-add field at the top of To do, 'No date' in the date tab, and late shown as ring plus words. FIX Home: drop the second Next stop and tube from the left line, or fold Next up into Coming up's first row, so the plans start within the first screen. Rename 'Later Lately added' to 'Lately added'. On the phone, show Status and Settings as icons in the bar instead of behind 'More'.

b.titles: Best: 'What needs a plan?' (x14a-sill-cross) and 'Give Vera something to plan.' (x14a-plate-cross, x14a-waypoint-cross). The first is a question the family answers by typing, so it works as the box's label: it covers weekends, reminders and ideas, and it cannot be answered 'no'. The second is a plain imperative that names who hears you and what she does, so a first-time user knows the box sends to Vera. 'Tell Vera what to line up.' (listing) works but uses an idiom: a kid or a non-native speaker may not take 'line up' as 'plan'. 'What can we pencil in?' (pocket) is charming, but it is an idiom and tentative; it suggests only calendar entries, not reminders or ideas. 'What's on for us?' (folio) fails as the label of a box you write in: it reads as a question the page should answer, so a parent may expect to read, not type, and it hints at nothing about adding a reminder or an idea, though it does suit asking Vera what is on. Carried titles: 'What needs planning?' (sill carried) is good but longer than the cross's; 'Tell Vera our plan.' (waypoint carried) presumes the family already has a plan.

b.notes:
The crosses beat their carried parents in every line, by 0.3 to 0.7 through this lens, and all of them changed page content, not just colour. The heat is not near-identical: rail and sill, plate seams, the diary line, the route arcs, the stem, contents lines.

Grafts that worked:
- Sill took Desk Terminal's instrument Status and made it its own (a faceplate with a lamp board plus a needle).
- Waypoint took Quote Board's head rows and Backlit Plate's rule heads; they now read as Waypoint's typesetting.
- Plate took the one day numeral from Waypoint, and it ties Home's rows, To do's due column and Plans together well.
- Pocket's ledger beside the meter.
- Listing's stem from the Sill line is a real tie between the light and the data.

Grafts that read pasted:
- Listing's round dials on Plans and Status sit alone in the head column like badges.
- Plate's brass placards are too faint to function.
- Folio's 'lit prompt' status line on the glass reads terminal-costume.
- The footer shape legends on Sill and Waypoint (from Dessau) are long, mostly empty strips at every page's foot: one per site at most.

Skeptic flags:
- Blue-steel plate caps and starter notches (Sill, Plate, Trued) drift toward navy.
- Amber rings repeated down Pocket's line read as a warning column.
- Waypoint's multicoloured kind squares read as confetti.
- Folio's greyed Fraunces title has no signature spark.
- Green share is still high on Plate (69%) and Sill (62%); the light is concentrated, not glaring, so I did not mark them down heavily.

The camps: the tour lines arrive more systematic per page (one line or rail on every page). The main lines arrive with better instruments and typesetting. The best crosses (Sill, Waypoint) are where a tour structure took main-camp head rows and instruments.

scores.why: Still the Matrix: green on near-black cards all the way down, mono everywhere, glow everywhere, so the light means nothing. Settings and To do are uniform boxed grids.

A strong joined system (one terminal with the question on the glass, Ready foot, NOW in lists), but the VT323 question in a box reads like an editor theme. Whole phrases in letterspaced mono ('was due 5 days ago') still shout, and Home is dense with no headline.
A clear rail with lit NOW and plates under it, a calm To do and Status. But the plates' blue-steel caps lean navy, the Status lamp board is small, and the greeting is a small card with no spark.
The plate law is sound, but on screen it is plain. 'mind' barely blooms, the long slate sheet has no seams, Status is a bare column under a small screen in the corner, and Settings is restyled only.

Now it reads as a plate: engraved seams, the round radar window cut over Next up's corner, a slot trace for plans and for To do's dates, and Status's spend and 30-day trace joined in one bevel are real page-content changes. The 'leak' under 'plan' reads as a stray dash or underline, the 12px brass placards are too faint to read, and the month view is still a plain grid.
A tidy listing grid, but flat. Bands of slate rows with a figure in the head column read as an admin table, and the tube floats unrelated beside the box.

The stem running from the tube down to Coming up's NOW is a real idea that ties the light to the data. Its square jog reads as a circuit-board trace, though, and the head-column figures ('4 PLANS', '12 IDEAS') sit isolated in a 13rem gutter. The title 'line up.' carries a two-word halo blob. Ideas and To do keep big empty left columns of filter keys.
The '900'/'990' thin folios are costume and the Home grid is a wall of boxed cells; only its Fraunces figure-setting earns its keep.

Much calmer: contents lines with leaders, Status rebuilt well, Fraunces drive figures on Ideas, a lit today on the month. But the title is set in a greyed Fraunces where the lit 'on' is two letters and has no spark. Serif plus VT323 plus Plex plus small caps is four voices. The '100/200/300' suffixes in the nav are still costume noise, and Home remains a dense mosaic.

The headline and wire onto the rail are bold, but the eight-letter lit 'planning' is a glow block. Plates are crowded under the board, and the dashed runs and branch ticks add drawing without meaning.

The best Home and Status in the heat. The page reads question, box, starters on a steel branch, then the Next tube and plates standing on a lit sill. Status is a real instrument faceplate (lamp board plus a needle meter with an amber zone). Weak points: the plate caps' blue lean, a long empty legend rail at every foot, and To do and Lately still boxed as panels.
One line of time is coherent, but Home stacks two monitors and the dashed tails are noisy. 'What's our plan?' asks the page to show rather than inviting input.

The steel line with rings now carries every page. Plans pairs its diary list with a tiny lit month on glass, a lovely touch, and Status's meter beside its ledger reads well. But amber rings repeat down the line until late looks like a warning column, the right column on Home is three boxed panels, the type is small throughout, and the phone puts Next below the fold.
The waypoint arcs and day numerals are a real drawing of the family's month. But the readout strip and Home's mono labels lean cockpit costume, and Ideas is a plain card list.

Large condensed head rows ('Things to do 4 open / 3 late') are the best typesetting here. The route arcs with ringed numerals that lead each row, and the month ringing each plan, change the page content itself. Ideas' two-column list with coloured square bullets reads as confetti, and the month's dotted stubs between weeks are clutter. Its title duplicates Plate's word for word.

fixes.suggestion: Keep: the question, box and steel branch of starters; the Next tube and plates standing on the lit sill with numerals hanging below; the Status faceplate (lamp board plus needle meter); the Chat track. Fix: take the blue (#86a9cc) out of the plate caps and use bone or steel, with the kind in its ring only, so Coming up stops reading navy. Unbox To do and Lately added on Home: put them on rule heads on the ground, as Settings now is. Cut the full-width legend rail at the foot to a short key at the left, or show it only on pages with lamps. On Status, give the five tally figures a rule above them so they are not loose under the faceplate. Show the To do 'Day' head on the page as well, or hide it on Home too, so both agree.

Keep: the head rows (Condensed title, bone figure, stacked mono unit), the four-week route with numerals in rings leading the rows, the readout strip, square ticks, and amber triangles for late only. Fix: on Ideas, drop the multicoloured square bullets and use one bone square, with kind as a word. On Plans month, drop the dotted leg stubs crossing week edges and keep only the lit leg today to Next. Fill Home's empty right column beside Coming up with the Google note and one 'Something to eat' line, or end the rows' measure there. Give it its own title: 'Give Vera something to plan.' is already Plate's.

Keep: the engraved seams, the round radar window cut over Next up, the slot traces on Home and To do (due dates as marks around Now), and Status's joined spend and 30-day trace with the lamp strip. Fix: delete the leak bar under 'plan', which reads as an underline or typo; let the pool spill without a shape. Lift the brass placards to 13px at a readable contrast, or cut them to one per page. Carry the cut grammar into the month: a lit slot per week, or cut only today's cell and each plan's numeral. The starter keys' blue-steel notches lean navy, so use bone.

Keep: the one steel line with rings on every page, the diary-set day tabs, and Plans' list with the small lit month on glass (the best new graphic in the heat). Fix: late should be one amber ring and the amber words, not a column of amber rings, so the line stops reading as a warning strip. Unbox Home's right column (To do, wishes, eat) onto the line as hairline groups. Raise the body type a step (rows are about 13px). On the phone, bring the Next tube above the starters, or shrink the box.

Keep: the lit stem from the tube to NOW, which is the heat's best cross-camp graft in idea, plus the round dials on Plans ('Next in 2 days') and Status. Fix: draw the stem as a curve or a straight drop from the tube's foot, not a PCB-like right-angle jog. Collapse the 13rem head column on Ideas and To do, where it holds a wall of filter keys, and put filters in the band's head row. Change the title (see titles).

Keep: contents lines with leaders, the rebuilt Status, Fraunces figures (drive times, counts), the month's lit today, and the To do tally tube. Fix: set the title at full bone ink and give the lit word real weight, or choose a title whose lit word is the job. Drop the page-number suffixes from the nav (keep P-numbers in page heads only). Cut one voice: keep Fraunces for figures and titles, Plex for text and VT323 on glass, and drop the synthesized small caps. Give Home one headline region instead of the mosaic.

b.titles: The best is 'What needs a plan?' (Sill, Squared): it cannot be answered 'no', it covers reminders and wishes as well as weekends, and the short lit 'plan' sits right above the lit run that answers it. A close second is 'Give Vera something to plan.' (Plate and Waypoint): it is a clear invitation that names who hears it, but two designs in one heat carrying the same words makes them near-duplicates at a glance, so one should take another title. 'What can we pencil in?' (Pocket, Lit) is charming and fits the diary, but it frames everything as tentative calendar entries; a reminder or a wish is not 'pencilled in', and six lit letters at display size is a heavy halo. These fail: 'Tell Vera what to line up.' (Listing): 'line up' reads as queueing or aligning, the lit run is two words, and it is a weaker echo of 'Tell Vera what to plan.' 'What's on for us?' (Folio) asks the page to show what is on, the opposite of the box's job, and its lit 'on' is too small to spark. Carried: 'What needs planning?' is a glow block, 'Tell Vera our plan.' presumes a plan exists, 'What's our plan?' asks to be shown, and 'What's on your mind?' is generic.
